book:web_bd7b938a.description: First volume of Isaac Deutscher's biography of Leon Trotsky, covering his life from birth through the Russian Revolution and Civil War.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Deutscher's book for an analysis of the relationship between party and Soviets during the October Revolution.

book:4899559.description: Few political figures of the twentieth century have aroused as much controversy as the Russian revolutionary Leon Trotsky. Trotsky's extraordinary life and extensive writings have left an indelible mark on revolutionary conscience, yet there was a danger that his name would disappear from history. Originally published in 1954, Deutscher's magisterial three-volume biography was the first major publication to counter the powerful Stalinist propaganda machine. In this definitive biography Trotsky emerges in hi...

book:web_df4fcfce.description: A detailed study of the Weimar Republic written from a socialist viewpoint, published in Zurich in 1933.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt notes Herzog's study as the most detailed recent work from a socialist perspective.
Hannah Arendt references Herzog's work for diary entries related to Hohenlohe.
Hannah Arendt cites Herzog's work for diary entries related to a specific date.

book:web_d93cff4f.description: Major work of Pan-Slavism by Nikolai Danilevsky (Danilewski), arguing for Slavic cultural and political unity against Western Europe. Originally published in Russian as 'Rossiya i Evropa'.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Danilewski's book as a foundational text of Pan-Slavism, quoting its praise of Russian political capacity.
Hannah Arendt references Danilewski's ideas on Pan-Slavic expansion, citing a previously mentioned work without repeating the title.

book:9654290.description:
Since there's never been a really good biography of Lenin in English, the idea of doing something about it came more or less simultaneously to three authors. As soon as each heard the others were at work, the race to get published was on. Stefan Possony won it, but Authors Payne & Fischer were close behind.
Each biography seems tailored to a specific audience. Robert Payne, a prolific & catholic writer, has produced a Book-of-the-Month selection aimed at romantics. Stefan Possony, political studies director...
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists these books as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_89977830.description: A German-language book about the rise of wealthy industrialists and entrepreneurs.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Lewinsohn's book as the source for the anecdote about the Rothschilds selling their Baku oil shares.

book:web_3b5dec6d.description: A historical study of Samuel Oppenheimer (1630-1703), a prominent Jewish banker and court factor to the Habsburg monarchy, and his financial circle. Published in 1913.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Grunwald's book on Samuel Oppenheimer for statistics on Jewish financial influence in Bavaria.

book:web_0dea6d40.description: An essay by French historian and essayist Daniel Halévy, published in the journal 'Cahiers de la Quinzaine' (Series 11, No. 10) in 1910. It reflects on the Dreyfus Affair and the political divisions in France.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Halévy's work regarding the creation of myths on both sides of the Dreyfus Affair.

book:1063799.description: This landmark study, first published by Cornell University Press in 1966, shows how Hitler's elite army grew from a praetorian guard of barely 28,000 men at the beginning of the Second World War to a combat-hardened army of more than 500,000 in 1945. George H. Stein examines in detail the structure and organization of the Waffen SS and describes the rigid personnel selection and intensive physical, military, and ideological training that helped to create the tough and dedicated cadre around which the larger...
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists a book by George H. Stein as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_99b5ecd0.description: A collection of material on the 'inner chronicle of the First World War' featuring writings by German soldiers and civilians, published by Yale University Press.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Hafkesbrink's book as a valuable collection on the atmosphere of World War I, noting the lack of similar studies for other countries.
Hannah Arendt lists a book by Fritz Thyssen as part of a bibliography or reference list.
Hannah Arendt references Thyssen's book as a source on economic aspects of Nazi support.

book:6767002.description:
(from the back):
ABSOLUTE DICTATOR OF THE THIRD REICH
This Brilliant evaluation of Hitler is drawn entirely from the records of his own times. The celebrated historian, Alan Bullock, has used every contemporary source, including the secret archives of the Third Reich and the records of the Nuremburg Trials, to produce this powerful, completely documented portrait-in-depth of the Nazi leader.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Bullock's work as the best study of Hitler and his career, noting its meticulous use of source material and comprehensive political background.
Hannah Arendt mentions Bullock's biography of Hitler as a later standard work, but suggests it is less accurate and relevant than the earlier account by Konrad Heiden.

book:529587.description:
"During the first two months of 1917 Russia was still a Romanov monarchy. Eight months later the Bolsheviks stood at the helm. They were little known to anybody when the year began, and their leaders were still under indictment for state treason when they came to power. You will not find another such sharp turn in history especially if you remember that it involves a nation of 150 million people. It is clear that the events of 1917, whatever you think of them, deserve study."
--Leon Trotsky, from History of...

book:184354.description: This priceless historical document by the Bolshevik leader features firsthand accounts from the top levels of the Russian revolutions of 1905 and 1917. Trotsky chronicles the struggle to consolidate a government run by workers and peasants, along with the rift between Lenin and Stalin and its political consequences.

book:184425.description: El presente libro esta consagrado a un problema estrechamente relacionado con la historia de las tres revoluciones rusas, pero no atane exclusivamente a ellas. Es un problema que durante los ultimos anos ha desempenado un papel inmenso en la lucha interna del Partido Comunista de la Union Sovietica, que ha sido luego trasplantado a la Internacional Comunista, que ha tenido decisiva importancia en el desarrollo de la revolucion china y que ha provocado una serie de resoluciones de importancia primordial resp...

book:953773.description:
One of Marxism's most important texts, The Revolution Betrayedexplores the fate of the Russian Revolution after Lenin's death. Written in 1936 and published the following year, this brilliant and profound evaluation of Stalinism from the Marxist standpoint prophesied the collapse of the Soviet Union and subsequent related events.
The effects of the October Revolution led to the establishment of a nationalized planned economy, demonstrating the practicality of socialism for the first time. By the 1930s, howe...

book:web_0785bdcf.description: A National Socialist legal treatise on the relationship between the Nazi Party and the German state, published during the Third Reich. The book presents the official party doctrine on the fusion of party and state apparatus.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt quotes a statement by Goebbels as recorded in Neesse's book to demonstrate the Nazi priority of party over state.
Hannah Arendt references Neesse's book for the official Nazi perspective on the political struggle against the 'system' and the Communist Party.

book:web_e9417cb3.description: A scholarly work analyzing the political and social ideas of French Catholicism, including discussion of the Dreyfus Affair. Published in Mönchengladbach (abbreviated as M. Gladbach).
commentaries: Hannah Arendt notes that Gurian also discusses the Dreyfus case in another of his books.

book:web_ede4e190.description: A documentation about the SS (Schutzstaffel), the paramilitary organization under Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists a book by Raimund Schnabel as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_51a1550a.description: A multi-volume ethnographic work on Jewish customs, history, and contemporary life by German Christian Hebraist Johann Jacob Schudt. The first volume was published in 1714, with subsequent volumes appearing through 1717.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Schudt's work as a source of information on Jewish matters.

book:web_9adcd673.description: Historical work by French Catholic priest and historian Édouard Lecanuet, examining the precursors to the 1905 French law on the Separation of the Churches and the State. Published posthumously in 1930.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Father Edouard Lecanuet's book for information on precursors to the separation of church and state.

book:web_9588f1be.description: A book about the Sturmabteilung (SA), the paramilitary wing of the Nazi Party, published in Berlin in 1938.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Ernst Bayer's book 'Die SA' in a footnote, quoting from its translation in 'Nazi Conspiracy'.
Hannah Arendt cites Bayer's book as the source for a Hitler speech from 1936, in which Hitler affirmed the symbiotic relationship between himself and the SA.

book:web_6053462a.description: Memoir by Alexander Terentyevich Vassilyev, the last head of the Tsarist Okhrana (secret police), detailing its operations and history. Published in English translation in 1930.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists a book by A. T. Vassilyev as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_07152a89.description: Memoirs of Felix Kersten, Heinrich Himmler's personal physician, detailing his experiences and observations of the Nazi regime.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt uses Kersten's book to provide a direct quote from Hitler, showing his contempt for party members who advocated for legal guarantees and a new legal order.

book:web_8e101aef.description: A scholarly work documenting the complicity of German academics and universities in Nazi ideology and the Holocaust, based on captured German documents.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt uses Weinreich's book as a source for a letter by Wilhelm Kube regarding the treatment of Jews.

book:web_f71cda6c.description: A comprehensive history of France from the French Revolution through the Third Republic, written by the Scottish historian and political commentator Sir Denis William Brogan.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt considers Brogan's work to contain the best political and historical evaluation of the Dreyfus Affair.
Hannah Arendt references Brogan's work for further details on Jacques Reinach and Cornélius Herz.
Hannah Arendt cites Brogan again regarding the replacement of Lévy-Crémieux by Reinach in the Panama Company.

book:5499968.description:
This book is a unique account by a survivor of both the Soviet and Nazi concentration camps: its author, Margarete Buber-Neumann, was a loyal member of the German Communist party. From 1935 she and her second husband, Heinz Neumann, were political refugees in Moscow. In April 1937 Neumann was arrested by the secret police, and executed by the end of the year. She herself was arrested in 1938.
In Under Two DictatorsBuber-Neumann describes the two years of suffering she endured in the Soviet prisons and in th...
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Buber-Neumann's book for a comparative testimony on the behavior of guards in Soviet versus Nazi camps.

book:162174.description: Jean-Paul Sartre was one of the most important philosophical and political thinkers of the twentieth century. His writings had a potency that was irresistible to the intellectual scene that swept post-war Europe, and have left a vital inheritance to contemporary thought. The central tenet of the Existentialist movement which he helped to found, whereby God is replaced by an ethical self, proved hugely attractive to a generation that had seen the horrors of Nazism, and provoked a revolution in post-war thoug...
commentaries: Susan Sontag critiques Sartre's view of literature as presented in his book 'What Is Literature?', describing it as instrumental and leading to a conformist sentiment.

book:30514.description: Jean-Paul Sartre's famous autobiography of his first ten years has been widely compared to Rousseau's Confessions. Written when he was fifty-nine years old, The Words is a masterpiece of self-analysis. Sartre the philosopher, novelist and playwright brings to his own childhood the same rigor of honesty and insight he applied so brilliantly to other authors. Born into a gentle, book-loving family and raised by a widowed mother and doting grandparents, he had a childhood which might be described as one long l...
commentaries: Susan Sontag refers to Sartre's book 'The Words' as a perfect account of his love for literature.

book:123933.description:
Jean-Paul Sartre, the great French existentialist, displays his mastery of drama in NO EXIT, an unforgettable portrayal of hell.
The play is a depiction of the afterlife in which three deceased characters are punished by being locked into a room together for eternity. It is the source of Sartre's especially famous and often misinterpreted quotation "L'enfer, c'est les autres" or "Hell is other people", a reference to Sartre's ideas about the Look and the perpetual ontological struggle of being caused to see...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Sartre's play No Exit as a foundational text illustrating how human relationships become sources of torment when the Other is perceived as intolerable.

book:511340.description: Jean-Paul Sartre, the seminal smarty-pants of mid-century thinking, launched the existentialist fleet with the publication of Being & Nothingnessin 1943. Tho the book is thick, dense & unfriendly to careless readers, it's indispensable to those interested in the philosophy of consciousness & free will. Some of his arguments are fallacious, others are unclear, but for the most part his thoughts penetrate deeply into fundamental philosophical territory. Basing his conception of self-consciousness loosely on H...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Sartre’s Being and Nothingness as the definitive philosophical account of self-deception, using it to introduce the concept of bad faith as a monadic form of lying.

book:web_9ae1e4a6.description: A collection of essays by French nationalist writer and politician Maurice Barrès, exploring nationalist doctrines and political scenes in late 19th-century France.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Barrès's book as a source on nationalist doctrines.

book:552008.description:
At the beginning of the Second World War, Koestler was living in the south of France working on Darkness at Noon.After retreating to Paris he was imprisoned by the French as an undesirable alien even though he had been a respected crusader against fascism. Only luck and his passionate energy allowed him to escape the fate of many of the innocent refugees, who were handed over to the Nazis for torture and often execution.
Scum of the Earthis more than the story of Koestler's survival. His shrewd observation....
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Koestler's book as a source on conditions in French concentration camps.

book:20501596.description:
Originally written in German, but the German manuscript was lost & only the manuscript of the English translation survived.
Darkness At Noonstands as an unequaled fictional portrayal of the nightmare politics of our time. Its hero is an aging revolutionary, imprisoned & psychologically tortured by the Party to which he has dedicated his life. As the pressure to confess preposterous crimes increases, he relives a career that embodies the terrible ironies & human betrayals of a totalitarian movement masking i...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Koestler’s novel as a literary parallel to the psychological mechanisms of forced confessions in both witch trials and Stalinist purges.

book:13576144.description:
Pre-ISBN
Bringing the history of cosmology--from the Babylonians to Newton--to life in a masterly synthesis, Koestler shows how the modern world-view replaced the medieval world-view in the scientific revolution of the seventeenth century.

commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists two books by B. H. Sumner as part of a bibliography or reference list.

commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists this book as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:21258721.description:
"Max Havelaar: Or the Coffee Auctions of the Dutch Trading Company" is a culturally and socially significant 1860 novel by Multatuli (the pen name of Eduard Douwes Dekker) which was to play a key role in shaping and modifying Dutch colonial policy in the Dutch East Indies in the nineteenth and early twentieth century. In the novel, the protagonist, Max Havelaar, tries to battle against a corrupt government system in Java, which was a Dutch colony at the time.
Eduard Douwes Dekker (2 March 1820 - 19 February...
commentaries: Hannah Arendt mentions Multatuli's book as a critique aimed at the Dutch government's exploitation in the East Indies.
Susan Sontag cites Multatuli's novel as an instance of verbose narration expressing acute mental distress.

Journalist Konrad Heiden was one of the first to hear the young Adolf Hitler's rousing orations and to recognize his political ingenuity and perverse, self-serving ideology.
As a staff reporter on the Frankfurter Zeitung Heiden was one of the first writers to take a stand against Naziism, and his is the only contemporary document to give the whole story of Hitler's rise to power from the very beginning to the day in 1934 when the Blood Purge eliminated the last opposition, leaving hom absolute dictator of G...

Hannah Arendt references Heiden's book to describe Hitler's character traits, such as untruthfulness and indifference to facts.
Hannah Arendt cites Heiden's book to illustrate the creation of shadow offices by the Nazis, paralleling the state with party organizations.
Hannah Arendt quotes Hitler's statement as recorded in Heiden's biography of Hitler.

book:web_fc038c15.description: Antisemitic work by Eugen Dühring presenting Jews as a racially harmful element to nations' existence, customs, and culture, with a historical response.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Duehring's book as an example of a leftist antisemitic work that introduced a naturalistic racial explanation of the 'Jewish question'.

book:web_f362b4d2.description: A scholarly article published in the collection 'Forschungen und Versuche zur Geschichte des Mittelalters und der Neuzeit' (1915), examining the Jewish policies of princely absolutism in the 17th and 18th centuries.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Priebatsch's work on Jewish policy under princely absolutism for an anecdote about a Jewish financier.

book:web_2cbd7185.description: Edited collection of secret SS Security Service (SD) reports on German public opinion during World War II, published by Heinz Boberach in 1965.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites this edited collection of secret reports as a revealing source on German public opinion during the war.

book:web_b4b19f2c.description: A biography of George Nathaniel Curzon, 1st Marquess Curzon of Kedleston, covering his final years as British Foreign Secretary and his failed bid to become Prime Minister.

book:web_ca17b629.description: A dissertation about Georg Ritter von Schoenerer, an Austrian pan-German nationalist politician who influenced later nationalist movements.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Neuschaefer's dissertation as a source on Georg von Schoenerer and Bismarck's attitude toward Austria.

book:web_f65ec003.description: Pamphlet by Russian Jesuit and writer Prince Ivan Gagarin, arguing for the potential conversion of Russia to Catholicism. Published in Paris in 1856.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Gagarin's pamphlet attacking Slavophiles.

book:web_3c5996df.description: Major sociological work by Georg Simmel, containing his influential chapter 'Sociology of Secrecy and of Secret Societies' which was later translated into English in various collections.

book:web_f8abd849.description: A biography of Georges Clemenceau, the French statesman who served as Prime Minister of France during World War I. This work is part of a multi-volume biography by journalist Georges Suarez.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Suarez's biography of Clemenceau.

book:web_d951e2ba.description: Memoirs by French far-right political theorist Charles Maurras, detailing his political life, the Dreyfus Affair, and the founding of the monarchist, nationalist movement Action Française.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites this book by Maurras as a source for theories related to the political life and the Dreyfus Affair.

book:web_8c386a22.description: A scholarly work analyzing the development and structure of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union during the Stalinist and post-Stalinist periods, focusing on the mechanisms of totalitarian control.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites this book for information about mass executions discovered during German occupation.

book:6351885.description: The 120 Days of Sodom by Marquis de Sade relates the story of four wealthy men who enslave 24 mostly teenaged victims and sexually torture them while listening to stories told by old prostitutes. The book was written while Sade was imprisoned in the Bastille and the manuscript was lost during the storming of the Bastille. Sade wrote that he "wept tears of blood" over the manuscript's loss. Many consider this to be Sade crowning achievement.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Sade's work as an extreme example of excessive revelation, contrasting it with Dante's restraint to illustrate narrative excess in feuilletons.

book:189776.description: Rosa Luxemburg was a revolutionary socialist who fought and died for her beliefs. In January 1919, after being arrested for her involvement in a workers' uprising in Berlin, she was brutally murdered by a group of right-wing soldiers. Her body was recovered days later from a canal. Six years earlier she had published what was undoubtedly her finest achievement, The Accumulation of Capital- a book which remains one of the masterpieces of socialist literature. Taking Marx as her starting point, she offers an....
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Luxemburg's work to support an analysis of the political structure of imperialism and its dependence on non-capitalist strata.

book:web_ccac0af0.description: A French-language collection of political memoirs, official correspondence, and unpublished documents of Konstantin Pobedonostsev, covering the period 1881-1894. Published in Paris in 1927.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt references Pobyedonostzev's memoirs to illustrate the concept of the suspect through a story about the Okhrana.

book:web_6c9e46e1.description: A collection of political essays by Konstantin Pobedonostsev, translated into English and published in London in 1898, expressing conservative and anti-liberal views.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt quotes from this book to illustrate Hannah Arendt's views on the nature and burden of power.

book:web_cc10448c.description: A scholarly work by historian Salo Wittmayer Baron examining the relationship between modern nationalist movements and religious identity, particularly in the context of Jewish history.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt quotes from this book to provide a source for a statement by M. N. Katkov.

book:web_bd6f3d9c.description: A historical and political analysis of Russia covering the period from the Russo-Japanese War to World War I, written by the German historian and politician Otto Hoetzsch. The work discusses Russian geopolitics, Pan-Slavism, and foreign policy.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites Hoetzsch's book to note Pan-Slavism's precedence in geopolitical thinking.
Hannah Arendt cites this as the standard work on the bureaucratization of party machines.

book:web_89ff4bed.description: A comparative analysis of Italian Fascism and German National Socialism, focusing on their economic and social policies. Published by Macmillan in New York.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists this book as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_3dfbf4ec.description: Autobiographical memoir by Ernst Röhm, chief of staff of the Nazi SA (Sturmabteilung), published in 1933. The title translates to 'The Story of a Traitor' and reflects Röhm's perspective on his political struggles.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt quotes from Röhm's book to show Nazi recognition of ideological common ground with Communists in the late 1920s.
Hannah Arendt quotes from Röhm's book to illustrate the rebellious feelings of the younger generation against bourgeois society.

book:web_d14a4d14.description: A historical study of the Bolshevik movement and the rise of communism in Russia by Polish-American historian Adam Ulam.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists two books by Adam B. Ulam as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_c06bcef4.description: A series of articles published in Revue Juive de Genève (issues 48, 49, 50, 1937) analyzing Marcel Proust's relationship to Judaism and assimilation.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites van Praag's article on Marcel Proust, but since it's an article in a journal, it should be excluded. I will remove it from the list.

book:web_d11840cc.description: A late 19th-century political analysis of Pan-Slavist agitation and South Slavic movements within the Austro-Hungarian Empire, published in Berlin.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists a book by Bresnitz von Sydacoff as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_bf6060de.description: Political work by Arthur Moeller van den Bruck that introduced the term 'Third Reich' and influenced Nazi ideology, arguing for a German empire distinct from both the Holy Roman Empire and the German Empire.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt cites this book as an example of the vague and grandiose rhetoric of Pan-Germanism.

book:web_bd22d628.description: A seminal historical study of Russian populist and socialist movements in the 19th century, originally published in Italian as 'Il populismo russo'.
commentaries: Hannah Arendt lists a book by Franco Venturi as part of a bibliography or reference list.

book:web_de4ba699.description: A comprehensive two-volume history of the Weimar Republic by German historian Erich Eyck, originally published in German as 'Geschichte der Weimarer Republik' and translated into English.

Jorge Luis Borges references Condorcet's book to explain its division of human history into stages and its posthumous publication.

book:146943.description: A new translation by Scot James Hogarth for the first unabridged English edition of the novel, which tells the story of a reculsive fisherman from the Channel Islands who must free a ship that has run aground in order to win the hand of the woman he loves, a shipowner's daughter.

book:9294773.description: Introducing one of the most famous characters in literature, Jean Valjean--the noble peasant imprisoned for stealing a loaf of bread--Les Miserables ranks among the greatest novels of all time. In it, Victor Hugo takes readers deep into the Parisian underworld, immerses them in a battle between good and evil, and carries them to the barricades during the uprising of 1832 with a breathtaking realism that is unsurpassed in modern prose. Within his dramatic story are themes that capture the intellect and the e...

book:1971935.description: With a cast spanning the doomed aristocracy and the suffering peasantry and including the warring revolutionary leaders Marat, Danton and Robespierre, Hugo brings to life the year 1793 - the year of the guillotine
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Hugo's novel Ninety-three as a central example of stylistic excess used to convey historical and moral conflict, praising its emotional intensity and symbolic depth.

book:45156.description: Sensational, dramatic, packed with rich excitement and filled with the sweep and violence of human passions, LES MISERABLES is not only superb adventure but a powerful social document. The story of how the convict Jean-Valjean struggled to escape his past and reaffirm his humanity, in a world brutalized by poverty and ignorance, became the gospel of the poor and the oppressed.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Hugo's Les misérables as the textual location where Hugo references Joseph de Maistre, using it to illustrate Hugo's complex justification of revolutionary violence through the lens of sacrifice and moral ambiguity.
Umberto Eco invokes this novel to contrast Hugo’s divine, omniscient narrative style with Stendhal’s limited perspective, highlighting Hugo’s use of historical events as metaphysical drama.

book:349376.description: Quasimodo, the hunchback bellringer of Notre-Dame Cathedral, is devoted to the beautiful gypsy dancer, La Esmerelda. When the demented archdeacon Frollo hatches a devilish plot to abduct La Esmerelda, Quasimodo will go to any lengths to protect the woman he loves.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites this novel to illustrate Hugo’s recurring motif of symbolic conflict between old and new forces, using Frollo’s famous phrase as a parallel to the guillotine’s symbolic role in Ninety-three.

book:8522696.description: This is a reproduction of a book published before 1923. This book may have occasional imperfections such as missing or blurred pages, poor pictures, errant marks, etc. that were either part of the original artifact, or were introduced by the scanning process. We believe this work is culturally important, and despite the imperfections, have elected to bring it back into print as part of our continuing commitment to the preservation of printed works worldwide. We appreciate your understanding of the imperfect...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Hugo’s preface to Cromwell as the theoretical foundation for Hugo’s literary treatment of the grotesque, linking it to Romantic aesthetics and the redefinition of beauty.
Umberto Eco cites Hugo’s preface to 'Cromwell' as the foundational Romantic text redefining the sublime through ugliness.

book:63038.description: Victor Hugo's The Man Who Laughs(first published under the French title L'Homme qui Ritin April 1869) is a sad and sordid tale -- not the sort of tale of the moment Hugo was known for. It starts on the night of January 29, 1690, a ten-year-old boy abandoned -- the stern men who've kept him since infancy have wearied of him. The boy wanders, barefoot and starving, through a snowstorm to reach a gibbet bearing the corpse of a hanged criminal. Beneath the gibbet is a ragged woman, frozen to death. The boy is a...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites 'The Man who Laughs' as a literary embodiment of the aestheticization of deformity and its erotic and philosophical implications.

book:7861910.description: This is a pre-1923 historical reproduction that was curated for quality. Quality assurance was conducted on each of these books in an attempt to remove books with imperfections introduced by the digitization process. Though we have made best efforts - the books may have occasional errors that do not impede the reading experience. We believe this work is culturally important and have elected to bring the book back into print as part of our continuing commitment to the preservation of printed works worldwide.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Victor Hugo's 'Légendes des Siècles' as a later French work attempting to combine two encyclopaedic structural tendencies.

book:5002395.description: Andrew Lang (1844-1912) was a prolific Scots man of letters, a poet, novelist, literary critic and contributor to anthropology. He now is best known as the collector of folk and fairy tales. As a journalist, poet, critic and historian, he soon made a reputation as one of the ablest and most versatile writers of the day. Lang was one of the founders of the study of "Psychical Research," and his other writings on anthropology include The Book of Dreams and Ghosts (1897), Magic and Religion (1901) and The Secr...
commentaries: Joseph Campbell references Lang's book as an introduction to the subject of the bull-roarer.

book:24874332.description:
'People begin to see that something more goes to the composition of a fine murder than two blockheads to kill and be killed - a knife - a purse - and a dark lane...'
In this provocative and blackly funny essay, Thomas de Quincey considers murder in a purely aesthetic light and explains how practically every philosopher over the past two hundred years has been murdered - 'insomuch, that if a man calls himself a philosopher, and never had his life attempted, rest assured there is nothing in him'.
Introducing....
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges contrasts criollo attitudes with De Quincey's satirical essay, which treats murder as an aesthetic subject.

book:1035331.description:
With an Introduction and Notes by David Ellis, University of Kent at Canterbury.
In the first part of this famous work, published in 1821 but then revised and expanded in 1856, De Quincey vividly describes a number of experiences during his boyhood which he implies laid the foundations for his later life of helpless drug addiction.
The second part consists of his remarkable account of the pleasures and pains of opium, ostensibly offered as a muted apology for the course his life had taken but often reading....
commentaries: Harold Bloom states that Borges's methods and themes are closely aligned with those of De Quincey, specifically referencing his works 'Confessions of an English Opium-Eater' and 'Suspiria de Profundis'.

book:web_fc0b9ec5.description: A work of literary criticism and aesthetics by philosopher Benedetto Croce, focusing on the nature and theory of poetry.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges quotes from a later work by Croce to show a more hostile view of allegory as cryptography.
Umberto Eco cites Croce's book as a foundational text distinguishing poetic moments from structural elements in literature, using it to frame the debate on imperfections and padding in poetry.

book:479709.description:
A reprint of the Library of Liberal Arts edition of 1965.
Croce's Guidepresents one of the clearest and strongest defenses of the intuitive nature of art in Western philosophical thought.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Croce's 'Estetica' as a work analyzing allegory and later quotes from it to explain Croce's rejection of allegorical art.

book:web_c290073d.description: A foundational history of aesthetics by the Italian philosopher Benedetto Croce, originally published in 1928, tracing the development of aesthetic thought from antiquity to the modern era.
commentaries: Umberto Eco includes Croce’s 1928 work as one of the classic histories of aesthetics encountered in the Treccani’s references, implying its relevance to the historical development of aesthetic theory.

book:web_86ee03a8.description: Philosophical dialogue by Giordano Bruno expounding his cosmological and metaphysical ideas, including the infinity of the universe and the unity of all substance.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges quotes a specific passage from Bruno's book 'Delia causa, principio ed uno' to illustrate his cosmological views.

book:web_d0528557.description: Philosophical dialogue by Giordano Bruno, first published in 1584 in London. The title translates to 'The Ash Wednesday Supper' and presents Bruno's Copernican cosmology and metaphysical ideas.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Bruno's work 'Cena de la ceneri' for its philosophical ideas on infinity and divinity.

book:web_87c815cd.description: A philosophical dialogue by Giordano Bruno, published in 1584, in which he presents a moral reform based on the triumph of celestial virtues over vices, using allegorical representations of constellations.
commentaries: Frances A. Yates describes the moral reform outlined by Bruno in his work 'Spaccio della bestia trionfante'.

book:web_ca0ce009.description: Major philosophical and theological work by Ramon Llull, presenting his combinatorial art (Ars Magna) for logically proving religious truths through systematic combination of concepts.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Llull's 'Ars magna' as a contrasting philosophical or combinatorial system to Swift's satirical machine.

book:web_1608d5a2.description: A philosophical and theological work by Ramon Llull, originally written in Arabic, presenting a dialogue between a Gentile and three wise men (a Jew, a Christian, and a Muslim) about religious truth.
commentaries: Frances A. Yates references an illustration from Lullo's collected works, specifically from his book 'Liber de gentili et tribus sapientibus', as a source for an image.

book:23187762.description: Le Roman de la Rose: [de Guillaume de Lorris et Jean de Meung]: traduction libre et en vers / par Et. Huard (de l'Ile Bourbon)Date de l'edition originale: 1835"[Le roman de la rose (francais). 1835]"Ce livre est la reproduction fidele d'une oeuvre publiee avant 1920 et fait partie d'une collection de livres reimprimes a la demande editee par Hachette Livre, dans le cadre d'un partenariat avec la Bibliotheque nationale de France, offrant l'opportunite d'acceder a des ouvrages anciens et souvent rares issus d...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references the 'Roman de la Rose' as an example of an allegorical work that was once considered enchanting.

Erich Auerbach cites Jean de Meun's work as an example of literary expression of doctrines of nature that praised the instinctive life of sex, placing it in the context of theological crises preceding Boccaccio.

book:web_f9619c36.description: A multi-volume philosophical dictionary and critique of language by the German philosopher and journalist Fritz Mauthner. The first edition was published in 1910, with revised and expanded editions following. The 1924 edition referenced in Borges's text is a later, updated version.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Mauthner's philosophical dictionary as one of the sources consulted for information on John Wilkins.

book:8480891.description: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket is Edgar Allan Poe''s only complete novel, published in 1838. The work relates the tale of the young Arthur Gordon Pym who stows away aboard a whaling ship called Grampus. Various adventures and misadventures befall Pym including shipwreck, mutiny and cannibalism. The story starts out as a fairly conventional adventure at sea, but it becomes increasingly strange and hard to classify in later chapte.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges states that the subject of the essay was inspired by this book.
Jorge Luis Borges introduces this novel as another example of fiction, analyzing its secret theme of terror associated with whiteness and its dual plot structure.
Jorge Luis Borges, discussing Borges's view of Chesterton, mentions Edgar Allan Poe as a figure representing a certain nightmarish literary mode.
Jorge Luis Borges mentions Edgar Allan Poe as a stylistic influence on H.G. Wells's early storytelling.
Jorge Luis Borges lists Poe among the writers Borges discovered by age twenty.
Jorge Luis Borges references Poe as an author whose work is defined by the creation of horror.

book:12722433.description: "The Mystery of Marie Roget", often subtitled A Sequel to "The Murders in the Rue Morgue", is a short story by Edgar Allan Poe written in 1842. This is the first murder mystery based on the details of a real crime. It first appeared in Snowden's Ladies' Companion in three installments, November and December 1842 and February 1843.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Poe's story as an early example of the detective genre that focuses on abstract resolution.

book:6234638.description: Dive into this classic from the singular mind of Edgar Allan Poe, who is widely regarded as the master of short horror fiction. "The Fall of the House of Usher" recounts the terrible events that befall the last remaining members of the once-illustrious Usher clan before it is -- quite literally -- rent asunder. With amazing economy, Poe plunges the reader into a state of deliciously agonizing suspense. It's a must-read for fans of the golden era of horror writing.
commentaries: H.P. Lovecraft references Poe's story as a benchmark for comparing the atmospheric horror in Shiel's "The House of Sounds".

book:26395525.description: Fantasy and reality collide when an unnamed narrator believes his beloved wife, Ligeia, has risen from the dead. -Ligeia- was one of Edgar Allan Poe's first published short stories, and spurred much debate as to the symbolism of Ligeia's death and supposed resurrection. A pioneer of the short story genre, Poe's stories typically captured themes of the macabre and included elements of the mysterious. His better-known stories include -The Fall of the House of Usher-, -The Pit and the Pendulum-, -The Murders i...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Poe's 'Ligeia' as an example of a nineteenth-century story using the convention of two heroines, one dark and one light.

Northrop Frye contrasts Poe's story with Hawthorne's work, citing Poe as a more radical abstractionist who presents the mythical pattern of death and revival directly, without the displacement for plausibility.

book:web_b7a37cd1.description: A short story by Edgar Allan Poe, first published in 1842 in The Gift: A Christmas and New Year's Present. It is a romantic tale about a man's love for his cousin Eleonora and his subsequent vow to her.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Eleanora as an example of a 'prison-Paradise or unborn world' from which characters seek escape.

book:web_b90bdb03.description: A foundational and influential history of Italian literature by the critic and statesman Francesco De Sanctis, first published in 1870. It is considered a classic of literary criticism and historiography.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites de Sanctis's history of Italian literature as a source analyzing allegory.
Jorge Luis Borges references Verne by mentioning his book 'Hector Servadac' in a comparison of precursors to Wells.

book:1018951.description: Five Union prisoners escape from the seige of Richmond in a balloon, are blown off course and crash on an uncharted island. They must learn to rebuild a society for themselves while awaiting rescue.
commentaries: Verne's novel is cited as an example of a foreign text translated into other languages, used to explore the dynamics of source-text fidelity and target-language adaptation.

book:web_8578998e.description: A scholarly introduction to Dante's Divine Comedy, published in Zurich in 1946.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Theophil Spoerri's book 'Einfuhrung in die Gottliche Komodie' for an observation on Dante's meeting with Beatrice.

book:661798.description: One of the central texts of the Middle Ages, The Golden Legenddeeply influenced the imagery of poetry, painting and stained glass with its fascinating descriptions of saints' lives and religious festivals. By creating a single-volume sourcebook of core Christian stories, Jacobus de Voragine (c. 1229-98) attracted a huge audience across Europe. This selection of over seventy biographies ranges from the first Apostles and Roman martyrs to near-contemporaries such as St Dominic, St Francis of Assissi and St El...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges describes the book as a collection of ecclesiastical lore and notes its popularity in the late Middle Ages.
Joseph Campbell cites a hagiographical text as a source for a saint's tale.

book:824212.description:
Virginia Woolf's Orlando, "The longest and most charming love letter in literature," playfully constructs the figure of Orlando as the fictional embodiment of Woolf's close friend and lover, Vita Sackville-West. Spanning three centuries of boisterous, fantastic adventure, the novel opens as Orlando, a young nobleman in Elizabeth's England, awaits a visit from the Queen and traces his experience with first love as England, under James I, lies locked in the embrace of the Great Frost.
At the midpoint of the n...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges mentions Borges translated Woolf's book 'Orlando', citing it as a specific work he engaged with.

book:1142058.description:
Introduced by Angelica Garnett
Regarded by many as Virginia Woolf's masterpiece, this novel was written partially to exorcise her private ghosts. It traces the lives of six people who are almost imperceptibly revealed through the kaleidoscopic accumulation of their reflections on themselves and each other.
commentaries: Susan Sontag cites Virginia Woolf's novel *The Waves* as a great but criticized example of elegiac and lyrical fiction in English literature.
Northrop Frye cites Mrs. Dalloway as an example where a suicide functions as a 'point of ritual death' for the protagonist.
Northrop Frye references Virginia Woolf's 'Between the Acts' as a profound work that contrasts civilization's course with flashes of significant moments.
Northrop Frye cites Between the Acts as a concentrated treatment of the contemplative phase, where a play cycles through English history before an audience.

book:30248276.description: Throughout history, some books have changed the world. They have transformed the way we see ourselves - and each other. They have inspired debate, dissent, war and revolution. They have enlightened, outraged, provoked and comforted. They have enriched lives - and destroyed them. Now Penguin brings you the works of the great thinkers, pioneers, radicals and visionaries whose ideas shook civilization, and helped make us who we are.
commentaries: Harold Bloom mentions Woolf's polemical works in the context of feminist criticism.
Harold Bloom mentions Woolf's polemical works in the context of feminist criticism.

book:186844.description:
The serene and maternal Mrs. Ramsay, the tragic yet absurd Mr. Ramsay, and their children and assorted guests are on holiday on the Isle of Skye. From the seemingly trivial postponement of a visit to a nearby lighthouse, Woolf constructs a remarkable, moving examination of the complex tensions and allegiances of family life and the conflict between men and women.
As time winds its way through their lives, the Ramsays face, alone and simultaneously, the greatest of human challenges and its greatest triumph--...
commentaries: Harold Bloom references the character Lily Briscoe from Woolf's novel To the Lighthouse as part of a tradition of heroines.

book:web_cdbdcade.description: A monumental Baroque epic poem in 45,000 lines, telling the mythological story of Venus and Adonis. It is Marino's most famous work and a landmark of 17th-century Italian literature.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Marino's 'Adone' as a prior work that described gardens for the five senses, similar to Beckford's 'Vathek'.
Jorge Luis Borges cites Marino's 'Adone' as an example where an allegorical moral about pleasure and pain can be found.

book:web_f2b4b49a.description: A collection of lyric poetry by Italian Baroque poet Giambattista Marino, first published in 1623. It is renowned for its elaborate metaphors, sensuous imagery, and influence on the Marinist poetic style.
commentaries: Umberto Eco references Marino's La lira to illustrate how aesthetic ideals in poetry valorize deviation from conventional beauty, such as the allure of pallor in illness.

book:web_93dc3a95.description: A foundational work on Theravada Buddhism based on Pali sources by a British Wesleyan missionary and scholar who worked in Sri Lanka.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Hardy's work on Buddhism to note an appreciation for the legend's vividness.

book:web_a49de2b9.description: A collection of short stories by Isaac Babel about Jewish gangsters in the Moldavanka district of Odessa, featuring the character Benya Krik. The stories were written and published in the 1920s-1930s, with the first English translation appearing in 1955.
commentaries: Harold Bloom references Isaak Babel as the writer of a specific book, 'Tales of Odessa', noting its thematic connection to Borges's story.

book:849866.description:
You don't have to love math to enjoy a hand of cards, a night at the casino, or a puzzle. But your pleasure and prowess at games, gambling, and other numerically related pursuits can be heightened with this entertaining volume, in which the authors offer a fascinating view of some of the lesser-known and more imaginative aspects of mathematics.
A brief and breezy explanation of the new language of mathematics precedes a smorgasbord of such thought-provoking subjects as the googolplex (the largest definite n...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges predicts this book will join his list of frequently reread works, praising its lucid presentation of mathematical charms accessible to non-specialists.
Jorge Luis Borges cites this book by Kasner and Newman in a review context.

book:web_51da1d82.description: Volume in Deussen's comprehensive history of philosophy focusing on post-Vedic Indian philosophy, where he analyzes systems like the one referenced (likely Buddhism or similar denial of self-knowability).
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Deussen's book 'Nachvedische Philosophie der Inder' for its account of Indian philosophy on self-knowledge.

book:web_38dfc5cb.description: Treatise on wit and literary conceits, considered a major work of Baroque literary theory and rhetoric.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges identifies Gracian's work as a key poetic art of the Spanish Baroque.
Jorge Luis Borges mentions Gracián's criticism in relation to Góngora's literary approach.

book:web_0b4b425b.description: A philosophical allegorical novel in three parts, considered a masterpiece of the Spanish Baroque. It follows the journey of Critilo (the man of experience) and Andrenio (the natural man) through a symbolic world representing human life and society.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges describes Gracian's works, noting that El criticón was a favorite of Schopenhauer and contains Borgesian themes.

book:web_a305f261.description: Critical study of Jorge Luis Borges' literary works, originally published in Spanish as 'La expresión de la irrealidad en la obra de Jorge Luis Borges' and later translated/adapted into English as 'Borges the Labyrinth Maker'.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges describes the book's jacket design and later critiques its methodological approach to categorizing Borges's philosophical themes.

book:web_fde109ce.description: Major philosophical/theological work by John Scotus Eriugena, presenting a Neoplatonic system of nature divided into four categories. It was condemned and burned in 1225 but survived in manuscripts.

Jorge Luis Borges cites the philosopher Johannes Scotus Erigena's concept of 'Nihil' to draw a parallel with Shaw's creative nothingness.
Jorge Luis Borges references the philosophical doctrine of Erigena, comparing it to an idea from Shaw's play to support the argument about the unreality of evil and Nazism.

Jorge Luis Borges references Borges's comparison of Nazism's unreality to Erigena's hells in a political commentary.

book:1329564.description: True Christianitypresents a satisfying and sensible alternative to mainstream Christianity. The last book published by Swedish scientist-turned-seer Emanuel Swedenborg, it serves as both the keystone in the architecture of his theology and the summary of his far-reaching psychological insights. This volume, the first of two, provides unique answers to humankind's perennial questions about the nature of God and about Jesus--not only what his purpose was and how he fulfilled it, but why his life and death are...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Swedenborg's book to illustrate a visionary condemnation of speculative theology about God's pre-creation state.

book:web_3ddc45d8.description: A theological work by Emanuel Swedenborg detailing his visions and doctrines concerning heaven and hell, published in Latin in 1758.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Swedenborg's theological treatise on heaven and hell.
Jorge Luis Borges cites Swedenborg's treatise as expressing a doctrine similar to one found in a modern play.
Jorge Luis Borges cites this book as expounding a doctrine about Hell and Heaven that is similar to one found in Man and Superman.

book:web_94f804a6.description: A collection of Swedenborg's spiritual and theological writings, including 'Heaven and Hell', 'Divine Love and Wisdom', and other mystical treatises, often published in multi-volume sets by the Swedenborg Society.
commentaries: The excerpt mentions Borges writing a prologue for an edition of Swedenborg's mystical works, indicating his interest in mystical literature.

book:web_2b2e41b0.description: Second volume in Anatole France's four-volume series 'Histoire contemporaine' (1896-1901), a satirical chronicle of French provincial life and politics during the Third Republic.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges identifies 'Mannequin d’osier' as part of Anatole France's series 'Histoire contemporaine'.

book:2425582.description:
This is the testament of Paul Baumer, who enlists with his classmates in the German army of World War I. These young men become enthusiastic soldiers, but their world of duty, culture, and progress breaks into pieces under the first bombardment in the trenches.
Through years of vivid horror, Paul holds fast to a single vow: to fight against the hatred that meaninglessly pits young men of the same generation but different uniforms against one another... if only he can come out of the war alive
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges mentions Remarque's novel as a counterpoint to Kipling's work, specifically in the context of war literature.

book:web_e6a4b658.description: A historical occult novel by Gustav Meyrink, blending the story of English occultist John Dee with a contemporary narrative.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges reviews a specific book by Gustav Meyrink, 'Der Engel vom Westlichen Fenster', indicating a direct citation of the work.

book:web_ffb933b7.description: A critical historical analysis of Christianity by the Scottish freethinker, journalist, and historian John Mackinnon Robertson.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Robertson's book to support an observation about the Gnostics and their method of constructing divine hierarchies.

book:web_b251d036.description: A monumental 15-volume compilation of travel narratives and geographical accounts from around the world, edited and compiled by Prévost. It was published between 1746 and 1759 and became a standard reference work on global exploration during the Enlightenment.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references the 'Histoire Generale des Voyages' as a source through which Rousseau and Nietzsche understood barbarous, pastoral life, unlike Hudson's firsthand experience.

book:web_56ed31bc.description: Early scientific work speculating about the possibility of life on the moon and methods of space travel, written by John Wilkins, an English clergyman, natural philosopher, and founder of the Royal Society.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Wilkins's book as a historical example of speculation about lunar habitation and travel, linking it to the development of science fiction.

book:web_dd05dd64.description: A 17th-century work proposing a universal language and philosophical classification system, published by John Wilkins, a founder of the Royal Society.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Wilkins' book as his speculative work on creating a world language, noting its physical dimensions and year of publication.

book:13298131.description:
The Book of Wonder is the seventh book and fifth original short story collection of Irish fantasy writer Lord Dunsany, considered a major influence on the work of J. R. R. Tolkien, H. P. Lovecraft, Ursula LeGuin and others. It was first published in hardcover by William Heinemann in November, 1912, and has been reprinted a number of times since. A 1918 edition from the Modern Library was actually a combined edition with Time and the Gods.
The book collects fourteen fantasy short stories by the author.
Sourc...
commentaries: H.P. Lovecraft cites this collection as a key example of Dunsany’s mythopoeic horror, highlighting its eerie, fairy-tale-like entities that evoke cosmic dread through subtle suggestion.

book:web_b4b2d307.description: A Spanish translation (titled 'Paginas de historia y autobiografia') of selected historical and autobiographical writings by Edward Gibbon, published by the University of Buenos Aires in 1961.
commentaries: The excerpt lists this as a prologue written by Borges, indicating his engagement with Gibbon's historical and autobiographical work.
Harold Bloom lists Gibbon's historical work as a canonical text of great aesthetic interest.

book:web_3650c011.description: A biography of John Wilkins (1614-1672), English clergyman, natural philosopher, and founder of the Royal Society.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges mentions consulting this biographical work on John Wilkins while researching for his note.

book:899896.description: The stories of twenty of Shakespeare's most popular plays
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites 'Tales from Shakespeare' by Charles and Mary Lamb as a preposterous example of paraphrase, using it to illustrate how interpretation can distort the original form.

book:380793.description: Hadleyburg prides itself on a reputation of incorruptible citizens until an offended stranger vows revenge, trapping the most sanctimonious by letters promising a fortune. Also 14 short works of fiction and "truth": his reporter debut, rescue of shipwrecked sailors, his first lie comments on white lies, petition to Queen Victoria on taxes, "Esquimau Maiden's Romance", a detective story, and others.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges quotes Twain's book to support an argument against racism and the idea of a chosen people, using it as authoritative commentary.

book:141312.description: Mark Twain's brilliant 19th-century novel has long been recognized as one of the finest examples of American literature. It brings back the irrepressible and free-spirited Huck, first introduced in The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, and puts him center stage. Rich in authentic dialect, folksy humor, and sharp social commentary, Twain's classic tale follows Huck and the runaway slave Jim on an exciting journey down the Mississippi.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Twain's 'Huckleberry Finn' as an example of a novel where the hero and circumstances reciprocally change each other, similar to 'The Purple Land'.
Northrop Frye uses Huckleberry Finn to discuss the theme of freeing a slave and the ironic recognition scene in comedy.

book:1118948.description: In this mischievous yarn by Mark Twain, a Yankee mechanic named Hank Morgan is knocked unconscious in a fight and awakens to find himself at Camelot in AD 528. Brought before the Knights of the Round Table, he is condemned to death, but saves himself by using his nineteenth-century scientific knowledge to pose as a powerful magician. After correctly predicting an eclipse, Hank is made minister to King Arthur, and goes on to counsel him on such matters as gunpowder, electricity, and industrial methods. But w...

book:98935.description: "This book is the record of a struggle between two temperaments, two consciences, and almost two epochs. It ended, as was inevitable, in disruption. Of the two being here described, one was born to fly backward, the other could not help being carried forward..." Thus begins this remarkable chronicle of the division between generations. Goose was born in 1849 into a deeply religious household; both parents were pious member of the Plymouth Brethren, a narrow sect. This book, Gosse's masterpiece, was anonymou...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges states he is relying on a summary from Edmund Gosse's book because he could not find the original 'Omphalos'.

book:web_a0a5f548.description: A study of the language and jargon used by Spanish criminals in the late 19th century, written by criminologist Rafael Salillas.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Rafael Salillas' book to provide a counterexample of obscure Spanish slang, challenging Dr. Castro's claims about Argentine linguistic corruption.

book:web_8d7f2413.description: A prose work by John Donne defending the thesis that suicide is not necessarily a mortal sin. Written circa 1608 but published posthumously in 1644.

book:web_afb04fc5.description: A diary by French writer Léon Bloy, covering the years 1892-1895, first published in 1898.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Bloy's work 'Le mendiant ingrat' as a source from which he rescued versions of Bloy's conjecture.

book:web_cd72cd93.description: A novel by French Catholic writer Léon Bloy, published in 1911. The title translates to 'The Old Man of the Mountain' and is one of Bloy's later works of fiction.

book:web_70fc62f0.description: A book by suffragette and activist E. Sylvia Pankhurst advocating for the constructed international language Delphos, which she helped develop as part of the international language movement.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Pankhurst's book as a source consulted in his research on John Wilkins.

book:web_2dab9891.description: A foundational two-volume work on Buddhism by the German scholar Carl Friedrich Köppen. The first volume, published in 1857, is titled 'Die Religion des Buddha und ihre Entstehung'.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Koeppen's work to explain a theological development in the legend where apparitions are divine creations.

book:web_9a709219.description: A scholarly work by Jesuit missionary and sinologist Léon Wieger, presenting Chinese biographies of Buddha with translations and commentary.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Wieger's collection of Chinese Buddha biographies to illustrate another variation where apparitions are godly metamorphoses.

book:web_57c73833.description: Historical work by Argentine writer Leopoldo Lugones about the Jesuit missions in South America, particularly the Jesuit reductions in Paraguay and surrounding regions.

book:1114472.description: Las fuerzas extranas reune doce relatos y una teoria del cosmos que constituyen los cuentos fantasticos mas perfectos de la literatura castellana y aun de la literatura. book:958034.description: "Lewis is the ideal persuader for the half-convinced, for the good man who would like to be a Christian but finds his intellect getting in the way". --Anthony Burgess. The New York Times Book Review
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites C.S. Lewis's book as a further reference on the topic of suffering.
Jorge Luis Borges references Lewis's book as additional reading on the topic of suffering, following the citation from Bernard Shaw.

book:web_d59ed61d.description: A collection of translations by Dante Gabriel Rossetti of early Italian poetry, including works by Dante Alighieri and his contemporaries, with the poem 'Al cor gentil rempaira sempre amore' by Guido Guinizelli appearing on page 291 in the 1874 edition published by Ellis and White in London.

commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites a translated poem from an anthology.
Jorge Luis Borges mentions Machen's autobiography, 'The London Adventure,' as presenting a hypothesis akin to Bloy's regarding the symbolic nature of the external world.

book:web_8dbdf714.description: A short story by Arthur Machen, first published in 1915, blending mystical themes with the horror genre; it explores the return of ancient spiritual forces, tied to the Holy Grail legend and the context of World War I.
commentaries: H.P. Lovecraft cites this work as a transcendent example of mysticism emerging from horror, linking it to the Graal legend and the wartime context.

book:21039781.description:
Print Length: 40 pages
Lucian of Samosata (125-c.180) was a Greek satirist of Syrian or Assyrian extraction, and True History is perhaps his most well-known tale. In this tale, the protagonist visits the Moon, meets extraterrestrial creatures, and takes part in interplanetary warfare. This piece of fantastical fiction parodies many works such as Homer's Odyssey, and is certainly a contender for the title of earliest science fiction story.
Many people could be forgiven for thinking that concepts such as voya...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Lucian's 'True History' as an early example of a fictional lunar voyage containing marvelous descriptions.

book:web_8e2c2db2.description: A dialogue by Lucian of Samosata praising friendship, in which a Scythian named Toxaris recounts stories of Scythian heroes and their war against the Bosporan Kingdom.
commentaries: Edward Gibbon references Lucian's 'Toxaris' as a literary source for a historical conflict, while noting its potentially fictional character.

book:7029455.description: This classic work is a general introduction to Indian philosophy that covers the Vedic and Epic periods, including expositions on the hymns of the Rig Veda, the Upanisads, Jainism, Buddhism and the theism of the Bhagvadgita. From the Rig Veda to Ramanuja, Radhakrishnan traces the development of Indian philosophy as a single tradition of thought through the ages. The author showc...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Radhakrishnan's work to support a description of the Buddhist concept of momentary thought.
Jorge Luis Borges cites Radhakrishnan's book to present a Buddhist perspective on the brevity of life, referencing a specific volume and page.

book:web_94f4a8e3.description: A collection of supernatural stories and ghostly encounters compiled by Lord Halifax, published in 1936.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges reviews a specific book attributed to Lord Halifax, 'Ghost Book', indicating a direct citation of the work.

book:web_c144e47d.description: Ancient Greek compendium of myths and heroic legends, traditionally attributed to Apollodorus of Athens but likely compiled by an unknown author in the 1st or 2nd century CE. It is a primary source for classical mythology.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Apollodorus's Bibliotheke for a myth about Orpheus and the sirens.

book:1935834.description: La obra de Quevedo editada aqui ha gozado a lo largo de los siglos de popularidad y tambien de consideracion controvertida. Los estudiosos se han planteado diversas cuestiones sobre la datacion, la fijacion del texto, la adscripcion o no al genero picaresco, la organizacion estructural, el sentido y significados ultimos de esta incomparable obra de ingenio. Domingo Yndurain traza en la introduccion un extenso panorama de estos problemas y de las distintas soluciones e ilustra el texto con abundantes y sabia...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges mentions Quevedo's 'Buscón' as an example of a purely successive narrative, criticizing Hudson for deviating from this simplicity in 'The Purple Land'.

book:69797.description: Tras haberse ejercitado en el modelo estructural de la picaresca de El Buscon, el mensaje de Quevedo, cada vez mas angustiado, se encauza en el genero de las visiones, de ascendencia tanto clasica como cristianomedieval. Con una satira cruel, repasa el universo de los vicios y pone de manifiesto su pesimismo radical sin solucion aparente.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Quevedo's book 'Sueño de la muerte' as an early use of the metaphor comparing dreams to theater.

book:3182098.description:
Boethius composed De Consolation Philosophiaein the 6th century while awaiting death by torture, condemned on a charge of plotting against Gothic rule, which he protested as manifestly unjust. Though a Christian, Boethius details the true end of life as the soul's knowledge of God, and consoles himself with the tenets of Greek philosophy, not with Christian precepts.
Written in a form called Meippean Satire that alternates between prose & verse, Boethius' work often consists of a story told by Ovid or Horac...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Boethius's 'De consolatione Philosophiae' as a work whose author would not share the modern disdain for allegory.
Jorge Luis Borges references Boethius's 'De Consolatione Philosophiae' as a source for the Wheel of Fortune metaphor, suggesting Layamon could have used it if he had contemplated cyclical conquest.

book:web_7fe4ff44.description: A periodical publication by Samuel Taylor Coleridge, later collected into a single volume, containing essays on philosophy, politics, and literature. The 'Essay on Method' appears in the 1818 edition.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references an essay by Coleridge from this work, while noting his interpretation may not be strictly correct.

book:web_436ef14a.description: A collection of Coleridge's critical writings edited by Thomas Middleton Raysor, published by Harvard University Press in 1936.
commentaries: Northrop Frye directs the reader to Coleridge's collected criticism, noting an expansion of Coleridge's idea to clarify a critical principle.

book:web_17ea1505.description: A collection of elegiac love poems by the Roman poet Propertius, written in the 1st century BCE.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges notes that Quevedo's line is a recreation or exaltation of a line from Propertius's 'Elegies'.

book:115775.description:
The most famous work of Japanese literature and the world's first novel--written a thousand years ago and one of the enduring classics of world literature.
Written centuries before the time of Shakespeare and even Chaucer, The Tale of Genjimarks the birth of the novel--and after more than a millennium, this seminal work continues to enchant readers throughout the world. Lady Murasaki Shikibu and her tale's hero, Prince Genji, have had an unmatched influence on Japanese culture. Prince Genji manifests what w...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges discusses the translation of Murasaki's work, praising its naturalness and psychological depth, and comparing it to European literature.

book:web_662a5722.description: Historical work by Argentine writer and historian José María Ramos Mejía, analyzing the era of Juan Manuel de Rosas. The book contains controversial claims about the Jewish-Portuguese origins of many Buenos Aires families.
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Ramos Mejia's book as a source listing family names to support a claim about Jewish ancestry in Buenos Aires.

book:814393.description: Dionysius of Halicarnassus was born before 53 BCE and went to Italy before 29 BCE. He taught rhetoric in Rome while studying the Latin language, collecting material for a history of Rome, and writing. His "Roman Antiquities" began to appear in 7 BCE. Dionysius states that his objects in writing history were to please lovers of noble deeds and to repay the benefits he had enjoyed in Rome. But he wrote also to reconcile Greeks to Roman rule. Of the 20 books of "Roman Antiquities" (from the earliest times to 2...
commentaries: Edward Gibbon cites a specific volume and page from Dionysius Halicarnassus's work on Roman antiquities as a footnote reference.

book:698911.description: Las ensenanzas del TAO TE CHING o <>, atribuido a LAO TSE (ca. s. v a.C.), pertenecen al amplio acervo de las sabidurias orientales antiguas. La esplendida version del poeta, traductor y estudioso practicante del zen Stephen Mitchell que aqui se ofrece esta regida por la intencion de traducir, mas que las palabras de la obra fundacional del taoismo, su idea. La complementariedad de los opuestos, el equilibrio, la obtencion de la plenitud mediante el desapego, la entrega al Tao, o absoluto, mediante el aband...
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites a specific verse from Lao-tse's foundational Taoist text.

book:3075730.description: Journalist, novelist, poet, artist and art critic, essayist, theologian, propagandist, philosopher, and creator of the wily old Father Brown - G. K. Chesterton is one of the most beguiling authors of the early twentieth century. When asked to perform a lecture tour in 1921, Chesterton was in a slump of depression. He had recently lost his brother to the First World War and his wavering faith in the face of the horrors of the conflict only intensified his malaise. 'What I Saw in America' tells us as much abo...

book:174852.description: A prolific and popular writer, G. K. Chesterton (1874-1936) is best known as the creator of detective-priest Father Brown (even though Chesterton's mystery stories constitute only a small fraction of his writings). commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges lists this book as an example of Chesterton's repeated use of a particular narrative formula.

book:1011931.description:

commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges lists this book as an example of Chesterton's repeated use of a particular narrative formula.

Jorge Luis Borges references Chesterton's book as an example of literary imagination concerning wicked or unnatural forms.

book:web_6a8c7fc0.description: A critical survey of American literature from colonial times to the early 20th century, originally published as 'Expression in America' in 1932.

book:web_39279196.description: A collection of mystery stories featuring the Old Man in the Corner, a detective character created by Baroness Orczy. commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Orczy's work as a recent example of the detective story that similarly avoids physical action.

book:web_26907f78.description: A philosophical work by Josiah Royce, originally delivered as the Gifford Lectures, exploring metaphysical and epistemological issues concerning the individual and the absolute.

commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references Gilson's book as a source for further reading on the scholastic commonplace regarding the two books.

commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites Ascasubi's book of gauchesco poems and provides its full title.

commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges notes Borges translated Faulkner's 'The Wild Palms', highlighting its influence on Latin American novelists.

book:1828986.description:

commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges references al-Mutanabbi's 'Diwan', identifying the poet and his dates.

book:21538250.description:
El Pollo Anastasio, un gaucho mitomano y conversador, recrea la historia del doctor Fausto para su amigo Laguna.
Alentado por la siesta morosa del bajo porteno, un oportuno porron de ginebra y el interes cada vez mayor que le demuestra su companero, el Pollo se ira entusiasmando hasta hacer una traslacion completa del drama, que de seguro Goethe no hubiera sonado, aunque si celebrado.
Con adecuadas dosis de humor, reducciones a la propia cultura y atractivas disgresiones, el Pollo nos cuenta el viejo mito d...
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges describes Estanislao del Campo's 'Fausto' as a poetic dialogue involving gauchos at an opera performance.

book:web_ad13f796.description: Book of poetry by Symbolist poet Gustave Kahn, notable for its early use of vers libre (free verse).
commentaries: Jorge Luis Borges cites a specific book of poetry by Gustave Kahn, noting its publication year and Jorge Luis Borges's role as a theorist.

book:web_e3d847a3.description: A dictionary of jargon and slang of the Buenos Aires underworld, published in 1915. It is referenced by Borges in his essay collection as 'The Language of the Populace' (Spanish: 'El lenguaje del bajo fondo').

book:230872.description: This work tells the story of Christian and his unique spiritual pilgrimage from the City of Destruction to the Celestial City. book:web_a3fc6fd7.description: A novel by Swedish author Gustaf Janson, originally published in 1935. The citation appears to contain a typographical error ('Komme1' instead of 'Kommer').
