book:103362.description:
The 15th edition of The Chicago Manual of Stylehas been superseded by the 17th edition.
In the 1890s, a proofreader at the University of Chicago Press prepared a single sheet of typographic fundamentals intended as a guide for the University community. That sheet grew into a pamphlet, and the pamphlet grew into a book--the first edition of the Manual of Style, published in 1906. Now in its fifteenth edition, The Chicago Manual of Style--the essential reference for authors, editors, proofreaders, indexers, c...
commentaries: Umberto Eco references the Chicago Manual of Style as a foundational text in American academic standards, contrasting its formal codification with Eco’s more personal, method-driven approach.
Umberto Eco suggests Eco’s methodology may have been influenced by the widespread adoption and revision of the Chicago Manual of Style, positioning it as a contextual backdrop to his work.

Umberto Eco contrasts the widespread use of the Chicago Manual with the deep, immersive reading of Eco’s book, implying Eco’s work offers more than procedural guidance—it provides intellectual formation.
Umberto Eco references this style guide as the authoritative source for adapting citation formats used in the book, particularly for English-speaking students.
Umberto Eco cites the Chicago Manual of Style as the editorial foundation for the translation, indicating its authoritative role in shaping stylistic decisions.

book:1317750.description: The epitome of symbolist drama. "Count Villiers de I'lsle-Adam", wrote Yeats, "swept together words behind which glimmered a spiritual and passionate mood, as the flame glimmers behind the dusky blue and red glass in an Eastern lamp". Paralleling the author's own metaphysical studies (which moved from occultism to more orthodox idealisms and back to Catholicism), these positions were examined by his characters. Each is rejected, and it is with the dramatic discovery of the highest ideal that the work ends.
commentaries: Umberto Eco references this translated work as an example of literary material used in the context of citation practices, though without elaborating on its thematic relevance.
H.P. Lovecraft cites this work as a prime example of the conte cruel, highlighting its extreme emotional torment and its status as a pinnacle of macabre short fiction.

book:web_ce3bda67.description: A seminal study by Italian art historian Eugenio Battisti exploring the conceptual and stylistic connections between Renaissance and Baroque art and literature, particularly focusing on metaphor and poetic expression in visual arts.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Battisti’s book as a crucial study connecting literary metaphor with baroque art, providing interdisciplinary insight into the period’s aesthetics.

book:web_04e2a5dd.description: A 1968 publication by Richard Braun, published by Fink in Munich, focusing on logic and epistemology. No widely recognized public figure or major academic work by this exact title and author is documented in major bibliographic databases, suggesting it may be a lesser-known or specialized academic work.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Braun’s book as an example of a well-known opinion used in academic debate, emphasizing the importance of correctly attributing claims to avoid confusion.

book:web_2d516d65.description: A foundational French-language introduction to generative grammar by Belgian linguist Nicolas Ruwet, published in 1967 by Plon in Paris. It was later translated into English by Norval S. H. Smith as 'An Introduction to Generative Grammar' (1973).
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Ruwet's original French work on generative grammar as a foundational text, noting its translation but preserving the original author and publication date.

book:web_ece0a1ed.description: A foundational text in linguistics by Belgian structuralist and generative grammar scholar Nicolas Ruwet, offering an accessible introduction to Noam Chomsky's generative grammar framework. The 1973 English translation by Norval S. H. Smith was published by North-Holland.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites this book as a comprehensive summary of generative grammar, used to contextualize Chomsky's position.
Umberto Eco references this book as an example of a translated work, noting the original author while including translator information for completeness.

book:web_eff39c72.description: A Renaissance treatise on wit, rhetoric, and the sources of ingenuity, attributed to Matteo Peregrini, an Italian scholar and rhetorician. The work is part of the tradition of Renaissance manuals on eloquence and ingenium, closely related to the genre of 'acutezze' (witty sayings) popular in late 16th-century Italy.
commentaries: Umberto Eco treats Peregrini’s second treatise as a core primary source, indicating its theoretical importance despite its scarcity.

book:web_67e64d95.description: Cesare Vasoli was an Italian historian of philosophy and Renaissance studies. This essay, published in the volume 'Umanesimo e Rinascimento: Studi in onore di Eugenio Garin', is a seminal work on Renaissance aesthetics, originally appearing in 1970 as part of a Festschrift for Eugenio Garin.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Vasoli’s essay as a critical source on humanist and Renaissance aesthetics, particularly for its analysis of Aristotelian commentators and their influence on baroque thought.

book:web_9d01bdb7.description: A study on prophecy and reason in Renaissance thought, published by Guida Editori in Naples.
commentaries: Frances A. Yates references Vasoli's book in a footnote as a major contemporary study on Giorgi and his works.

book:281965.description: Knowledge and Belief An Introduction to the Logic of the Two Notions by Jaakko Hintikka Prepared by Vincent F. Hendricks & John Symons In 1962 Jaakko Hintikka published Knowledge and Belief: An Introduction to the Logic of the Two Notions with Cornell University Press. Almost every paper or a book on epistemic and doxastic logic that has appeared since then has referred to this seminal work. Although many philosophers working in logic, epistemology, game-theory, economics, computer science and linguistics m...
commentaries: Umberto Eco references Hintikka's book 'Knowledge and Belief' as a theoretical foundation used by Lucia Vaina-Pusca to support her analysis of Baudelaire's poem.

book:9232817.description: Interstellar travel to alien worlds is too expensive for Marvin, a college student in need of a good vacation. So he signs up for what he can afford: a mind swap, in which his consciousness is swapped into the body of an alien life-form. Unfortunately, Marvin finds himself in the body of an interstellar criminal--a body that he has to vacate, fast. But that criminal consciousness has stolen Marvin's earthly body. Now Marvin has to find a body on the black market just to stay alive! Travel with Marvin from w...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Sheckley’s novel as a concrete example of how science fiction depicts time warps as gateways to possible worlds, using it to illustrate note-taking methodology.

book:12569850.description: A la fin du XIXe siecle, par un froid dimanche de novembre, un garcon de quinze ans, Francois Seurel, qui habite aupres de ses parents instituteurs une longue maison rouge - l'ecole du village -, attend la venue d'Augustin que sa mere a decide de mettre ici en pension pour qu'il suive le cours superieur : l'arrivee du grand Meaulnes a Sainte-Agathe va bouleverser l'enfance finissante de Francois... Lorsqu'en 1913 parait le roman d'Alain-Fournier, bien des themes qu'il met en scene - saltimbanques, fetes enf...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Alain-Fournier’s novel as an example of a concise primary text suitable for direct annotation, contrasting it with more complex works.

book:6298312.description: In ill health following a stroke, Sir Walter Scott wrote 'Letters on Demonology and Witchcraft' at the behest of his son-in-law, J. G. Lockhart, who worked for a publishing firm. The book proved popular and Scott was paid six hundred pounds, which he desperately needed. (Despite his success as a novelist, Scott was almost ruined when the Ballantyne publishing firm, where he was a partner, went bankrupt in 1826.) 'Letters' was written when educated society believed itself in enlightened times due to advances...
commentaries: H.P. Lovecraft cites Scott's nonfiction work as a authoritative compilation of European witch-lore, highlighting its enduring scholarly value.

book:1448072.description: The heroic adventures of Sir Wilfred make Ivanhoeperhaps Scott's most unforgettable work: the fiery rescue of Sir Wilfred of Ivanhoe and his fellow captives from Knight Templar's castle by Robin Hood; the wounded Ivanhoe's trial by combat with the powerful Knight to save the lovely Jewess Rebecca from the stake; and King Richard the Lion-Hearted's aid in Ivanhoe's triumph at evil King John's tournament. To follow Sir Wilfred's spirited exploits is to enter the colorful era of medieval England, a world of ro...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites 'Ivanhoe' as an example of a nineteenth-century novel using the convention of two heroines, one dark and one light.

book:web_5b54374d.description: A seminal work by Italian philosopher Paolo Rossi examining the history of memory systems, symbolic logic, and the quest for a universal language from the Renaissance to the early modern period, particularly focusing on figures like Ramon Llull, Francis Bacon, and Leibniz.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Paolo Rossi's book as an example of ambiguous citation practices due to insufficient author identification.

book:web_8f478d69.description: A guide to writing term papers, co-authored by C. W. Cooper and E. J. Robins, published in its 4th edition by Stanford University Press in 1967.
commentaries: Umberto Eco references this manual as a practical guide for term paper writing, using it to support advice on thesis structure.

book:9672479.description: Pubblicato presso l'editore Laterza nel 1966, "Storia dell'Italia partigiana" e il primo libro "di storia" del giornalista Giorgio Bocca. Gia inviato tra i piu importanti del paese, Bocca inizia con questo volume una tradizione di scrittura storiografica che conta numerosi titoli e che Feltrinelli intende riproporre al pubblico di oggi. Scritta con la felicita di racconto e l'acutezza nell'osservazione e nella descrizione del grande cronista, questa Storia spicca per l'equilibrio dello sguardo e per la chia...
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Bocca's historical account as a primary source for understanding the political divisions within the Italian Resistance during World War II.

book:web_dee6a413.description: An essay by Yuri Lotman, a prominent Russian-Latvian semiotician and literary theorist, originally published in the collection 'Russian Poetics in Translation', Volume 3, edited by Lawrence M. O'Toole and Ann Shukman. The essay explores semiotic structures in artistic texts through the conceptual dichotomy of 'beginning' and 'end'.
commentaries: Umberto Eco cites Lotman’s essay within the edited volume as a specific example of semiotic analysis, emphasizing the need to trace its original Russian publication for scholarly precision.

book:15823473.description:
In intimate and eloquent interviews, including the last he gave before his suicide, the writer hailed by A.O. Scott of The New York Timesas "the best mind of his generation" considers the state of modern America, entertainment and discipline, adulthood, literature, and his own inimitable writing style.
In addition to Wallace's last interview, the volume features a conversation with Dave Eggers, a revealing Q&A with the magazine of his alma mater Amherst, his famousSalon interview with Laura Miller following...

book:6748.description: In this exuberantly praised book - a collection of seven pieces on subjects ranging from television to tennis, from the Illinois State Fair to the films of David Lynch, from postmodern literary theory to the supposed fun of traveling aboard a Caribbean luxury cruiseliner - David Foster Wallace brings to nonfiction the same curiosity, hilarity, and exhilarating verbal facility that has delighted readers of his fiction, including the bestselling Infinite Jest.
commentaries: The book is cited alongside Consider the Lobster as a notable collection of Wallace’s nonfiction essays.

book:1152876.description: Do lobsters feel pain? Did Franz Kafka have a funny bone? What is John Updike's deal, anyway? And what happens when adult video starlets meet their fans in person? David Foster Wallace answers these questions and more in essays that are also enthralling narrative adventures. Whether covering the three-ring circus of a vicious presidential race, plunging into the wars between dictionary writers, or confronting the World's Largest Lobster Cooker at the annual Maine Lobster Festival, Wallace projects a quality...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references his own published work as the container for the McCain campaign essay, indicating its significance as a collected piece of nonfiction.
The book is mentioned as a collected nonfiction work by Wallace, indicating its significance in his literary output.

book:745905.description:
One of the outstanding voices of his generation, David Foster Wallace has won a large and devoted following for the intellectual ambition and bravura style of his fiction and essays. Now he brings his considerable talents to the history of one of math's most enduring puzzles: the seemingly paradoxical nature of infinity.
Is infinity a valid mathematical property or a meaningless abstraction? The nineteenth-century mathematical genius Georg Cantor's answer to this question not only surprised him but also sho...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references his own book as a source of ideas about mathematicians in popular culture and the myth of the 'mad genius.'

book:1152877.description:
A gargantuan, mind-altering comedy about the Pursuit of Happiness in America. Set in an addicts' halfway house and a tennis academy, and featuring the most endearingly screwed-up family to come along in recent fiction, Infinite Jestexplores essential questions about what entertainment is and why it has come to so dominate our lives; about how our desire for entertainment affects our need to connect with other people; and about what the pleasures we choose say about who we are.
Equal parts philosophical ques...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace is cited as the creator of Infinite Jest, described as his most famous work and a defining text of his career.

book:6438.description:
One of David Foster Wallace's most famous essays, now available as an eBook short.
Beloved for his keen eye, sharp wit, and relentless self-mockery, David Foster Wallace has been celebrated by both critics and fans as the voice of a generation. In this hilarious essay, originally published in the collection A Supposedly Fun Thing I'll Never Do Again, he chronicles seven days in the Caribbean aboard the m.v. Zenith. As he partakes in supposedly fun activities offered on the luxury tour, he offers riotous ane...

book:965463.description: The winner of the PEN/Faulkner Award for fiction writes a memoir that brings to life the stuff of boyhood--from paper routes to whiskey, fistfights to friendship and betrayal--and captures as well America in the fifties.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace mentions Tobias Wolff's 'This Boy’s Life' in passing, associating it with Frank Conroy's work as part of a group of admired nonfiction writers.

book:11534772.description:
With the release of Roberto Bolano's The Savage Detectives in 1998,journalist Monica Maristain discovered a writer "capable of befriending his readers." After exchanging several letters with Bolano, Maristain formed a friendship of her own, culminating in an extensive interview with the novelist about truth and consequences, an interview that turned out to be Bolano's last.
Appearing for the first time in English, Bolano's final interview is accompanied by a collection of conversations with reporters statio...
commentaries: Bolaño’s interview is presented as a volume in the series, implying his views on literature and legacy are being honored as significant.

book:1788759.description: Ava Klein, thirty-nine, lover of life, world traveler, professor of comparative literature, is dying. From her hospital bed on this, her last day on earth, she makes one final ecstatic voyage. People, places, offhand memories, and imaginary things drift in and out of Ava's consciousness and weave their way through the narrative. The voices of her three former husbands emerge: Francesco, a filmmaker from Rome; Anatole, lost in the air over France; Carlos, a teenager from Granada. The ways people she loved ex...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Carole Maso’s novel Ava as a work of extraordinary emotional power, as described by a friend.

book:103638.description: First published in 1967, Stop-Timewas immediately recognized as a masterpiece of modern American autobiography, a brilliant portrayal of one boy's passage from childhood to adolescence and beyond. Here is Frank Conroy's wry, sad, beautiful tale of life on the road; of odd jobs and lost friendships, brutal schools and first loves; of a father's early death and a son's exhilarating escape into manhood.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Frank Conroy's 'Stop Time' as a work by a personal hero, expressing admiration despite critical disagreement over his actions.
David Foster Wallace cites Stop-Time as a seminal literary memoir that inspired his own desire to become a writer, acknowledging its significance in his personal literary development.
David Foster Wallace references this novel as another example of literature that evokes a sophisticated, intellectually mediated form of emotional resonance.

book:11047557.description:
All three parts of the epic masterpiece The Lord of the Rings - The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers & The Return of the King - available as one download, featuring the definitive edition of the text, hyperlinked footnotes and page references, and 3 maps including a detailed map of Middle-earth.
Sauron, the Dark Lord, has gathered to him all the Rings of Power - the means by which he intends to rule Middle-earth. All he lacks in his plans for dominion is the One Ring - the ring that rules them all - w...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites 'The Lord of the Rings' as a culturally resonant reference point and praises it as an exceptionally engaging read, using its imagery to illustrate fleeting fame.

book:web_9d5eaed8.description: A classic children's story about a stuffed rabbit who becomes real through the love of his owner, first published in 1922. Though often misattributed to Margaret Wise Brown, the actual author is Margery Williams Bianco.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace describes this children’s book as the purest example of emotional impact, surpassing even complex literary works in its directness.

book:525225.description: Published to overwhelming critical acclaim, this remarkable collection of short stories established A. M. Homes as one of the most provocative and daring writers of her generation. Here you'll find the cult classic, "A Real Doll, " the tale of a teenage boy's erotic obsession with his sister's Barbie doll; "Adults Alone, " which first introduced Paul and Elaine, the crack-smoking yuppie couple whose marriage careens out of control in Homes's novel Music for Torching; and "Looking for Johnny, " in which a ki...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites A.M. Homes’ story 'A Real Doll' from The Safety of Objects as an effective teaching tool for students.
David Foster Wallace cites Homes’s novel as a defining example of Image-Fiction, using a pop-culture icon as the center of a psychological narrative.

book:14241.description: When it was published in 1995, Mary Karr's The Liars Clubtook the world by storm and raised the art of the memoir to an entirely new level, as well as bringing about a dramatic revival of the form. Karr's comic childhood in an east Texas oil town brings us characters as darkly hilarious as any of J. D. Salinger's--a hard-drinking daddy, a sister who can talk down the sheriff at twelve, and an oft-married mother whose accumulated secrets threaten to destroy them all. Now with a new introduction that discusse...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Mary Karr’s memoir as her most well-known work, while also praising her poetry.

book:28747.description:
Six short stories and a novella. Set in a dystopian near-future in which America has become little more than a theme park in terminal disrepair, they constitute a searching and bitterly humorous commentary on the current state of the American Dream.
Funny, sad, bleak, weird, toxic - the future of America as the Free Market runs rampant,the environment skids into disarray, and civilization dissolves into surreal chaos. These wacky, brilliant, hilarious and entirely original stories cue us in on George Saunde...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace praises George Saunders’ debut collection as a remarkable and deserving work.

book:1289275.description: Wittgenstein's Mistress is a novel unlike anything David Markson or anyone else has ever written before. It is the story of a woman who is convinced and, astonishingly, will ultimately convince the reader as well that she is the only person left on earth. Presumably she is mad. And yet so appealing is her character, and so witty and seductive her narrative voice, that we will follow her hypnotically as she unloads the intellectual baggage of a lifetime in a series of irreverent meditations on everything and...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites this novel as an example of top-shelf literary fiction that produces a complex, cerebrative kind of emotional impact.

book:298310.description: Twin Peaks creator David Lynch offers his many fans the chance to see the peculiar, private land of Lynch--sketches that led to many of his famous film images, short pieces of fiction, personal artwork, and photos of his unusual obsessions (spark plugs, dental surgery, bald women). 200 b/w illustrations. Two 16-page 4-color inserts.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Lynch's published book as an example of his multidisciplinary artistic output, noting its mixed aesthetic quality.

book:web_dc4cb993.description: A film directed by David Lynch, serving as a prequel to the television series 'Twin Peaks'. It explores the final days of Laura Palmer and is known for its surreal, dark tone.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Fire Walk with Me as a Lynch film whose character development enhances its emotional and psychological creepiness.

book:691383.description: Quentin Tarantino's films have single-handedly revived and redefined American noir, bringing to Hollywood a new energy, irony, and cool. Tarantino has won awards and accolades around the world, earned a devoted following among critics, actors, and audiences, and paved the way for a new generation of young filmmakers. Tarantino's directorial debut, Reservoir Dogs, hit the screen with a freshness and brutal edge that left critics and audiences stunned. The story of a heist gone wrong, the film weaves a taut a...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace treats Reservoir Dogs as a commercialized homage to Lynch’s style, specifically citing its ear-cutting scene as an explicit reference to Blue Velvet.

book:494739.description: The Spanish-American poet comments on the nature, communicative function, and evolution of modern poetry. Bibliogs.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Paz's Children of the Mire as a source of ideas, likely for its cultural or philosophical insights.

book:244942.description:
In The Bow and the Lyre Octavio Paz, one of the most important poets writing in Spanish, presents his sustained reflections on the poetic phenomenon and on the place of poetry in history and in our personal lives. It is written in the same prose style that distinguishes The Labyrinth of Solitude. The Bow and the Lyre will serve as an important complement to Paz's poetry.
Paz's discussions of the different aspects of the poetic phenomenon are not limited to Spanish and Spanish American literature. He is almo...
commentaries: Harold Bloom quotes from Paz's 'The Bow and the Lyre' regarding Paz's interpretation of Walt Whitman, which Harold Bloom considers 'beautifully mistaken'.

book:31941623.description:
Supplementary essay and interview collection to the 2005 Criterion Collection DVD release of My Own Private Idaho. Listed as "A 64-page book featuring new essays by JT LeRoy and film critic Amy Taubin, a 1991 article by Lance Loud, and reprinted interviews with Van Sant, Phoenix, and Reeves."
The book is organized and presented as...
Prologue - Dramatis Personae
Act I - "Private Places" by Amy Taubin
Act II - "Boise on the Side" by JT LeRoy
Act III - "Shakespeare in Black Leather" by Lance Loud
Originally a...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites My Own Private Idaho as a film using Lynchian dream logic to explore character psychology and subconscious desire.

book:163480.description: Author William H. Gass analyzes as though under a microscope the many and varied ways writers carpenter structures with words to house language forms. "Using Freudian concepts, he compares the art of writing to the art of becoming civilized: writing parallels the transformation of raw instinct into shared expression. . . . Gass writes with impassioned concern".--PUBLISHERS WEEKLY.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Gass's book to support an argument about the persistence of authorship despite theoretical attempts to eliminate David Foster Wallace's role.

book:287031.description:
The new Miramax Film Four Roomsmarks the rapid ascent of four immensely talented writer-directors: Allison Anders, Alexandre Rockwell, Robert Rodriguez, and Quentin Tarantino.
Here, each of them write and direct a segment of the nightmare that is Ted the bellhop's first night at the front desk. He's caught in a comedic maze, careening from a coven of witches to a couple with psychosex on their minds and firearms at the ready. Then he's off to babysit a threatening gangster's rambunctious kids. And finally h...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Four Rooms as a film outside Lynch’s oeuvre, used as a negative contrast to highlight Lynch’s superior artistry.

book:774783.description: A new collection of interlocking short fictions that pay an irreverent and entertaining fictional tribute to Hollywood myths, from the acclaimed author of The Public Burning and Gerald's Party.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Coover’s A Night at the Movies as a post-1985 Image-Fiction text that engages with cinematic and televisual culture.
David Foster Wallace cites Coover’s You Must Remember This as part of the Image-Fiction wave, treating media and memory as intertwined themes.

book:web_31021535.description: A short story by Robert Coover, originally published in 1977 in the collection 'Pricksongs and Descants'. It is a postmodern, experimental narrative that exemplifies Coover's innovative style and use of mythic and folkloric motifs.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Coover's novel as an early instance of Imagist tactics, positioning it within the evolution of Image-Fiction.

book:530741.description: Three screenplays by Mike Leigh. Naked presents a bleak picture of urban society, Life is Sweet is a gentle comedy in which the pain of everyday life is borne with a wry smile, and High Hopes is a comedy of class-ridden life in contemporary Britain.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Naked as a film employing Lynchian narrative disjunction through its use of unrelated, unsettling parallel storylines.

book:web_95acbc3c.description: A 1990 book by George Gilder, a prominent technology futurist and conservative thinker, in which he predicts the rise of interactive media and the decline of traditional broadcast television, emphasizing the role of bandwidth and digital networks in transforming American life.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Gilder's book as a representative example of technologically optimistic conservative thought on television, highlighting its commercial packaging and flawed assumptions about consumer agency and technological solutions.
David Foster Wallace cites Maya Deren as an influence on Lynch’s experimental, dreamlike cinematic language.

book:22571704.description: In 1975, Greil Marcus'sMystery Train changed the way readers thought about rock 'n' roll and continues to be sought out today by music fans and anyone interested in pop culture. Looking at recordings by six key artists--Robert Johnson, Harmonica Frank, Randy Newman, the Band, Sly Stone, and Elvis Presley--Marcus offers a complex and unprecedented analysis of the relationship between rock 'n' roll and American culture. In this latest edition, Marcus provides an extensively updated and rewritten Note and Disc...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Marcus's Mystery Train as a significant cultural analysis, likely for its insights into American music and identity.

book:716226.description:
The Language of the Hand
A brand-new edition of the classic work first published in 1894. Cheiro was a renowned palmist whose world travels gained attention in the press and whose palm readings for the rich and famous of his day, including Mark Twain, elicited words of praise. In this unique book are methods for reading personalities, recognizing astrological links, and prognostication, along with drawings of hands showing structural types and lines. A series of photographic hand prints taken directly from....
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Cheiro’s book as an effective airfoil for biking against the wind, suggesting he found unexpected practical value in a text likely intended for divination or palmistry.

book:16098650.description:
Librarian's Note: this is an alternate cover edition- ISBN 10: 0679745580 (ISBN 13: 9780679745587)
On November 15, 1959, in the small town of Holcomb, Kansas, four members of the Clutter family were savagely murdered by blasts from a shotgun held a few inches from their faces. There was no apparent motive for the crime, and there were almost no clues.
As Truman Capote reconstructs the murder and the investigation that led to the capture, trial, and execution of the killers, he generates both mesmerizing sus...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Truman Capote's In Cold Blood as the source of Robert Blake’s acclaimed 1967 performance, using it to highlight the depth and menace Lynch has revived in Blake’s role.

book:636175.description: The acclaimed author of Free Agents presents a brilliant satire involving a struggle for land in central Florida between three commercial giants; Walt Disney, Howard Johnson, and Margery Post.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace lists Apple’s Propheteers as a post-1985 example of Image-Fiction, highlighting its engagement with public figures and media.

book:490255.description: With this, his famous inaugural collection of stories, Max Apple dives into the mainstream of American culture, and his unfailingly wry depictions of the forces that drive this great nation (greed, lust, perfection, ice cream) make his stories exciting, frightening, and eternally new.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Max Apple’s short story as an early example of projecting interior life onto a pop-culture figure, foundational to Image-Fiction.

book:web_85a89045.description: A play by Bernard Pomerance, first performed in 1977, based on the life of Joseph Merrick, known as the Elephant Man. It was later adapted into a film by David Lynch in 1980.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references The Elephant Man as a major Lynch film that helped redefine cinematic boundaries during the 1980s blockbuster era.
David Foster Wallace cites Blood Simple as an example of a Coen Brothers film that employs Lynchian chiaroscuro lighting and noir aesthetics.

book:web_cd9d5f9b.description: A seminal work by Fredric Jameson analyzing the relationship between global capitalism, aesthetics, and film, arguing that postmodern cultural forms reflect the logic of late capitalism and geopolitical shifts in the post-Cold War era.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Jameson's books as examples of dense, obscure academic writing, using them to critique the style of contemporary literary scholarship.

book:web_70d50cd3.description: A seminal work of Marxist literary criticism by Fredric Jameson, analyzing structuralism and the limitations of language in literary theory. It critiques Saussurean linguistics and explores the ideological dimensions of narrative form.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Jameson's books as examples of dense, obscure academic writing, using them to critique the style of contemporary literary scholarship.

book:web_2e5f162d.description: A critical work by Fredric Jameson exploring the relationship between visual culture, ideology, and representation in film and media, focusing on how the visible is structured by historical and political forces.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace quotes this specific work to exemplify what he considers obscurantist academic prose, highlighting its syntactic confusion and stylistic excess.

book:310976.description: Since his death in 1989, John Cassavettes has become increasingly renowned as a cinematic hero--a renegade loner who fought the Hollywood system, steering his own creative course in a career spanning thirty years. Having already established himself as an actor, he struck out as a filmmaker in 1959 with Shadows, and proceeded to build a formidable body of work, including such classics as Faces, Woman Under the Influence, The Killing of a Chinese Bookie, and Gloria. In Cassavettes on Cassavettes, Ray Carney p...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Cassavetes as a key influence on Lynch’s raw, emotionally intense filmmaking style.

book:393601.description: Any book-length interview with Alfred Hitchcock is valuable, but considering that this volume's interlocutor is Francois Truffaut, the conversation is remarkable indeed. Here is a rare opportunity to eavesdrop on two cinematic masters from very different backgrounds as they cover each of Hitch's films in succession. Though this book was initially published in 1967 when Hitchcock was still active, Truffaut later prepared a revised edition that covered the final stages of his career. It's difficult to think o...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace acknowledges Hitchcock as one of Lynch’s cinematic influences, though no specific film is cited.

book:19170772.description: Reissued with an additional preface to sit alongside the volume on Stanley Cavell in Contemporary Philosophy in Focus this famous collection of essays covers a remarkably wide range of philosophical issues (there are essays on Wittgenstein, Austin, Kierkegaard, and the philosophy of language) and extends beyond philosophy into discussions of music and drama.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references a specific chapter of Cavell's book.

book:web_26d66344.description: A philosophical autobiography by American philosopher Stanley Cavell, published by Stanford University Press.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references this book for Cavell's reminiscences of conversations.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites a specific page from Cavell's book.

book:web_7d6d4218.description: A critical study of German cinema by British film historian and documentary filmmaker Paul Rotha, originally published as part of his broader work on film history. book:7756245.description: In the jungles of South America, on the ice fields of Alaska, the plains of the Midwest, and the streets of San Francisco, a fearsome battle rages. The insects are vying for world domination; the inventors of electricity stand in evil opposition. Bug , a young man, rebels against his own kind and joins forces with the insects. book:2065376.description: Here are 13 daring and innovative tales dealing with "skinheads, x-ray patients, whores, lovers, fetishists, and other lost souls" who populate landscapes as diverse as ancient Babylon, India, and contemporary San Francisco. commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Vollmann’s collection as Image-Fiction that anthropomorphizes consumer electronics, embedding them in philosophical frameworks.

book:1106138.description: Welcome to Mark Leyner'sAmerica, where you can order gallium arsenide sushi at a roadside diner, get loaded on a cocktail of growth hormones and anabolic steroids, and support your habit by appearing on TV game shows. book:web_f526067e.description: A collection of short stories by American writer Stephen Dixon, published in 1993 by Henry Holt and Company. The book features fragmented, emotionally intense narratives often exploring themes of loss, memory, and domestic life.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace references Dixon’s collection as an Image-Fiction work that explores the intersection of film and narrative form.

book:17669440.description: Ambrose Bierce is one of the most notable and influential American horror authors, bridging the period between Poe and Lovecraft. His spare precise prose and sardonic wit easily set him apart from a genre full of melodrama and purple prose. This is the second collection of his short stories published during his lifetime, and contains such classics of American horror as 'Haita the Shepherd', 'An Inhabitant of Carcosa', 'The Death of Halpin Frayser', and 'The Damned Thing'.
commentaries: H.P. Lovecraft cites this book as one of the two primary collections containing Bierce’s weird tales, establishing its canonical status in American weird literature.
H.P. Lovecraft cites this book as one of the two primary collections containing Bierce’s weird tales, establishing its canonical status in American weird literature.

book:440003.description: Krazy Kat adores Ignatz Mouse. She sees the bricks he hurls at her head as tokens of love, and each day Ignatz arranges a cunningly different method of delivery for his missile. But when Ignatz and Krazy witness the mega-brick explosion in the desert, Krazy becomes depressed, and refuses to perform. To coax her back to work so they can regain their lost limelight, Ignatz invents his own brand of psychotherapy, orchestrates her kidnapping, and tries to seduce Krazy with promises of stardom from a Hollywood p...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Cantor’s Krazy Kat as a post-1985 Image-Fiction work that reimagines pop-culture icons in literary form.

book:web_1cec2369.description: A scholarly work by H. L. Hix, originally published as a Ph.D. dissertation and later released as a book by Temple University Press in 1992 as part of their 'The Arts and Their Philosophies' series. It explores the death of the author in postmodern literary theory, engaging with thinkers like Barthes and Foucault.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Hix’s book as a significant 1990s critical work that engages with poststructuralist theory, particularly Barthes’ 'Death of the Author.'

book:web_14e710a9.description: A 1996 action-horror film written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by Robert Rodriguez. It is not a book but a movie, often referenced in pop culture discussions. The citation mistakenly treats it as a book, but it is a cinematic work.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites From Dusk to Dawn as a commercially driven film that lacks Lynch’s depth, used to underscore Lynch’s artistic superiority.

book:5988858.description: Three years on the New York Times bestseller list, CODEPENDENT NO MORE first identified attitueds, feelings, and behaviors now recognized as hallmarks of codependency. Checklists, activities, and self-tests provide concrete tasks to help readers examine the nuances of codependency in their lives.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace notes an older passenger reading this book, implicitly associating it with the emotional dynamics of cruise passengers, though without elaborating on its content or author's ideas.

book:web_292fb8bd.description: A 1994 American comedy film written, directed, and produced by the Coen Brothers. It stars Tim Robbins, Jennifer Jason Leigh, and Paul Newman. The film is a satirical homage to 1940s screwball comedies and corporate culture.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace includes The Hudsucker Proxy as another Coen Brothers film exhibiting Lynchian visual and tonal influences, particularly in lighting and mood.

John McCain is one of the most admired leaders in the United States government, but his deeply felt memoir of family and war is not a political one and ends before his election to Congress. With candor and ennobling power, McCain tells a story that, in the words of Newsweek, "makes the other presidential candidates look like pygmies."
John McCain learned about life and honor from his grandfather and father, both four-star admirals in the U.S. Navy. This is a memoir about their lives, their heroism, and the....

David Foster Wallace cites McCain’s memoir as a strategic component of his 2000 campaign, suggesting it was used to reinforce an image of authenticity while being part of a calculated marketing effort.

book:web_256f79f7.description: A comprehensive reference guide to modern legal terminology, usage, and style, widely regarded as an authoritative resource for lawyers, judges, and legal writers.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Garner's earlier dictionary as a foundational work that established his reputation in usage scholarship.

book:344645.description: This book - a detailed explanation and defense of standard American English - contains more than 700 pages of crisp, authoritative guidance on hundreds of questions of grammar and usage. "A Dictionary of Modern American Usage" treats all these topics and more: basic grammar, as well as advanced nuances; word preferences and shades of meaning; punctuation; idiomatic phrases; spelling; and effective style. In an age of linguistic uncertainty, this book gives surefooted guidance on the direct, precise, and rob...

Which is preferred - nom de plume, pseudonym, or pen name? What are neologisms, disguised conjunctions, and fused participles? Janet Whitcut has revised Eric Partridge's popular reference book to reflect the language of well-informed writers, readers, and speakers today. She has also added a section to the book entitled "Vo...
commentaries: David Foster Wallace describes Garner’s formative encounter with Partridge’s book as a pivotal moment that ignited his lifelong passion for English usage.
David Foster Wallace cites Partridge’s work as a direct descendant of Fowler’s influence in the usage guide tradition.

book:web_617325a1.description: A major American English dictionary published in 1961 by G. & C. Merriam Company, notable for its descriptive rather than prescriptive approach to language, which sparked controversy for including words like 'heighth' and 'irregardless' without usage labels.
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites Webster’s Third as a landmark event that ignited contemporary linguistic debates, framing it as a turning point in the authority of dictionary-making.

book:1002280.description: Six months on the men's professional tennis tour
commentaries: David Foster Wallace cites this book as a representative example of national media coverage on drug culture, using it to ground a broader observation about journalistic reporting.

book:web_5e0899ca.description: Autobiographical memoir by American tennis player Tracy Austin, ghostwritten by sportswriter Christine Brennan, detailing her rise to fame, Wimbledon and US Open victories, career-ending injury, and personal struggles.

book:web_b2a80e0b.description: A witty and authoritative critique of American English usage, grammar, and linguistic pretension by journalist and NBC news anchor Edwin Newman, originally published in 1974.

book:web_7afa486b.description: A scholarly study of the English court masque, tracing its development from medieval entertainments through its peak in the Jacobean and Caroline periods, examining its literary, dramatic, and social significance.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references this book as a source for a statement about something being said to be descended.

book:4331561.description: The second of Cooper's five Leatherstocking Tales, this is the one which has consistently captured the imagination of generations since it was first published in 1826. It's success lies partly in the historical role Cooper gives to his Indian characters, against the grain of accumulated racial hostility, and partly in his evocation of the wild beautiful landscapes of North America which the French and the British fought to control throughout the eighteenth century. At the center of the novel is the celebrat...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites 'The Last of the Mohicans' as an example of a nineteenth-century novel using the convention of two heroines, one dark and one light.

book:web_34531665.description: A scholarly study examining the development and characteristics of epic poetry in 19th-century French literature.
commentaries: Northrop Frye directs the reader to this book for further information on the epic in France.

book:web_53dc5de1.description: A series of essays on political economy by John Ruskin, first published as a book in 1872 after serialization in Fraser's Magazine (1862-1863).
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites a footnote from Ruskin's work as an example of an attempt at genuine criticism, interpreting Shakespeare through a personal conceptual framework.

book:web_1c4df506.description: A study of Greek mythology focusing on Athena, blending art criticism, mythology, and social commentary. Ruskin examines the symbolic meaning of Athena across Greek myths and connects these myths to contemporary Victorian society.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Ruskin's 'Queen of the Air' as a modern example of the allegorical explanation of myths.

book:138908.description: Two brothers rescue their sister from the spell of an evil magician.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Comus as an example of a moral allegory representing the defense of innocence against experience.

book:17678810.description:
Gulzar, one of India' finest film-makers and lyricists, has always been a poet at heart. His oeuvre is steeped in a poetic sensibility, marked by a lyricism rare in the world of Hindi cinema. Born in 1934, Gulzar's journey as a poet began with the Progressive Writers' Movement. Today, he is regarded as one of India's foremost Urdu Poets, unparalleled in his exploration of human relationships and the insights and sensitivity with which he addresses the many facets of daily life.
Whether evoking an abiding no...
commentaries: Northrop Frye references this specific edition for a poem ('Camellia Sabina'), noting textual variations in later editions.

book:web_a711a558.description: A pastoral play by Elizabethan dramatist George Peele, written as court entertainment celebrating Queen Elizabeth I. It features mythological characters and concludes with Paris presenting the golden apple to Elizabeth.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Peele's play 'Arraignment of Paris' as an example of a secular drama with parallels to religious mystery plays.

book:2541248.description: Volpone tells of a magnifico of Venice with no wife or children to whom to leave his fortune. The prospect of such wealth invites to his house an assortment of greedy hopefuls, ready to prostitute any ideals in the pursuit of money. Volpone's parasite, Mosca, assists him in milking these pretenders as they deserve. When Volpone and Mosca practice their schemes on innocent victims, however, the play turns in a more unpredictable direction and ends in a series of surprises. Subplot figures enrich the narrativ...
commentaries: Harold Bloom references characters from Jonson's plays, Volpone and The Alchemist, to illustrate unchanging character types.

book:1410532.description:
Acknowledged by T. S. Eliot as one of the chief sources for his great poem "The Waste Land," Jessie L. Weston's From Ritual to Romanceremains a landmark of anthropological and mythological scholarship. In this book she explores the origins of the Grail legend, arguing that it dates back to a primitive vegetation cult and only later was shaped by Celtic and Christian lore.
To prove her thesis, Weston unites folkloric and Christian elements by using printed texts to prove the parallels existing between each a...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book as the source for a claim ('we are told') in the narrative.

book:1853180.description:
More successful in its day than The Way of the World, which is now
accounted Congreve's best play, Love for Love (1695) is a comical farce manifesting the verbal polish and the theatrical wit that audiences so enjoy in Congreve. Valentine, Sir Sampson's dissolute eldest son, finds himself at a standstill; the only way out of his financial difficulties is to give in to his father's pressure to renounce his right of inheritance. While this suggestion immediately increases the chances of his bluff younger brot...
commentaries: Northrop Frye analyzes Love for Love to highlight Oedipal themes and comic infidelity in Restoration comedy.

book:7008439.description: William Congreve (1670-1729) was an English playwright and poet. He wrote some of the most popular English plays of the Restoration period of the late 17th century. By the age of thirty, he had written four comedies, including Love for Love (premiered 1695) and The Way of the World (premiered 1700), and one tragedy, The Mourning Bride (1697). After writing five plays from his first in 1693 until 1700, he produced no more as public tastes turned against the sort of highbrow sexual comedy of manners in which....
commentaries: Harold Bloom notes Johnson's lapse in praising a passage from Congreve's Mourning Bride above Shakespeare.

book:12414975.description: Breaking from Freud by allowing for nonsexual psychic forces driving the libido, Carl Jung made a more lasting name for himself than did his mentor. Psychology of the Unconsciousis a prodigious leap away from Freud's dictatorial constraints, exploring the mythic aspects of our interior lives in exquisite detail. While he sometimes sacrifices readability for erudition, this is no failing for the interested student, who strives to follow Jung as he moves from Norse mythology to Shakespeare to Sanskrit etymolo...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this work, noting it is soon to be retranslated, in a discussion of the hero archetype.

book:297544.description:
Verso la fine degli anni venti Jung scopre singolari affinita tra antichi simboli cinesi e i sogni dei suoi pazienti: comincia cosi a studiare i testi degli alchimisti. Dopo quindici anni di lavoro pubblica questo volume, che rimane fra i suoi testi piu affascinanti. La tradizione alchimistica e la pratica analitica hanno in comune il tentativo di creare una realta nuova e superiore: da una parte l'oro, la pietra filosofale, dall'altra la "presa di coscienza" della psicologia moderna.
L'alchimia e espressio...
commentaries: Joseph Campbell references Jung's book as a source for the discussion of religious ideas within alchemy.
Joseph Campbell provides a citation for specific paragraphs from this work on analytical psychology and symbolism.
Joseph Campbell cites specific paragraphs from Jung's work as a reference.
Northrop Frye cites this book as a source on alchemical symbolism.

book:11721378.description: When Carl Gustav Jung and Karl Kerenyi got together to collaborate on this book, their aim was to elevate the study of mythology to a science. Kerenyi wrote on two of the most ubiquitous myths, the "Divine Child" & "The Maiden", supporting the core "stories" with both an introduction & a conclusion. Jung then provided a psychological analysis of both myths. He defined myth as a story about heroes interacting with the gods. Having long studied dreams & the unconscious, Jung identified certain dream patterns....
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this collaborative work as further reading on mythological science.

book:123636.description: In this book, Dr. Jung, who has been the author of some of the most provocative hypotheses in modern psychology, describes what he regards as an authentic religious function in the unconscious mind. Using a wealth of material from ancient and medieval gnostic, alchemistic, and occultistic literature, he discusses the religious symbolism of unconscious processes and the possible continuity of religious forms that have appeared and reappeared through the centuries.
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites Jung's work to define archetypes and notes its original publication.

book:3223295.description:
Bollingen Series XX
Index & bibliography
Psychology of the Unconscious is an important early work of C.G. Jung, published as Wandlungen und Symbole der Libido in 1912. The English translation by Beatrice M. Hinkle appeared in 1916 under the full title of Psychology of the Unconscious: A Study of the Transformations & Symbolisms of the Libido, a Contribution to the History of the Evolution of Thought (London: Kegan Paul Trench Trubner). Jung published a revised version of the work, in German in 1952, transla...
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites Jung's book, providing publication details and noting its original title and translation history.

book:web_e6dcbfc8.description: A scholarly work examining the origins and development of ancient Greek comedy, particularly its ritual and mythological foundations.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references Cornford's book as the source for a suggestion regarding the structure of Old Comedy.
Northrop Frye cites this book for an analysis of thematic repetition in Forster's work.
Northrop Frye references Kierkegaard's book to illustrate the concept of 'repetition' as a creative and redemptive act, contrasting it with Platonic recollection.

book:9004295.description: In Timore e tremore Kierkegaard tenta di rispondere all'angoscioso dilemma della rinuncia, il sacrificio richiesto dalla ragione: la dimensione del silenzio e dell'assurdo pieno di solitudine e di sofferenza della fede, che <>. Raccontando la storia di Abramo e la paradossalita del sacrificio del figlio Isacco che gli viene chiesto da Dio, Kierkegaard mostra la radicalita dell'atteggiamento religioso. Una rassegnazione infinita e un credere nell'assurdo che inducono l'autore a porre il problema del rapporto...
commentaries: Harold Bloom suggests Kafka's interpretation of Abraham was a critical response to Kierkegaard's work 'Fear and Trembling'.

book:web_991320c7.description: A scholarly work by Gertrude Rachel Levy examining the origins and structures of epic literature, analyzing mythical epics, quest-epics, and conflict-epics. Published by Faber and Faber.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book to support a classification of epic frameworks, noting a correspondence with his own categories.

book:3146295.description:
Jane Ellen Harrison (9/9/1850-4/5/1928) was a British classical scholar, linguist & feminist. She's one of the founders, with Karl Kerenyi & Walter Burkert, of modern studies in Greek mythology. She applied 19th century archeological discoveries to the interpretation of Greek religion in ways that have become standard. Contemporary classics scholar Mary Beard, Harrison's biographer, has described her as "in a way...[Britain's] first female professional career academic".
Jane Harrison finished her major book...
commentaries: Northrop Frye notes that certain Greek terms come from an excursus in this book.
Northrop Frye references a specific account within this book concerning the 'eniautos-daimon' in the context of archetypal criticism.
Joseph Campbell quotes Jane Harrison's interpretation of a vase painting depicting the return of Jason, noting the dragon-slayer being born anew from the dragon's jaws.
Joseph Campbell references Harrison's book as a notable scholarly work on correspondences between Greek and Australian rites.
Joseph Campbell notes that Harrison's book cites a fragment of Aeschylus in its discussion.

book:web_0e86a86d.description: A seminal work by classical scholar Jane Ellen Harrison, arguing for the primacy of ritual over myth in ancient Greek religion. The 1922 edition cited is the third and final revised edition.
commentaries: Joseph Campbell references Harrison's scholarly work for its discussion of a verse from Euripides.

book:web_3f6b5d00.description: Comic opera in two acts, with libretto by W. S. Gilbert and music by Arthur Sullivan. It premiered in London in 1885 and satirizes British institutions and bureaucracy through a fictional Japanese setting.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references the operetta as a clearer example of ritualistic sacrifice themes than found in Aristophanes, highlighting its explicit parody elements.

book:55427.description:
This labyrinthine and extraordinary book, first published more than fifty years ago, was the outcome of Graves's vast reading and curious research into strange territories of folklore, mythology, religion and magic. Erudite and impassioned, it is a scholar-poet's quest for the meaning of European myths, a polemic about the relations between man and woman, and also an intensely personal document in which Graves explored the sources of his own inspiration and, as he believed, all true poetry.
This new edition...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Graves's book as a learned exposition of the cyclical symbolism associated with a female archetype.

book:46787.description: The narrative drive of Stowe's classic novel is often overlooked in the heat of the controversies surrounding its anti-slavery sentiments. In fact, it is a compelling adventure story with richly drawn characters and has earned a place in both literary and American history. Stowe's puritanical religious beliefs show up in the novel's final, overarching theme--the exploration of the nature of Christianity and how Christian theology is fundamentally incompatible with slavery.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references Stowe's novel as an example where the plot serves to illustrate a central theme, specifically slavery.
Harold Bloom mentions that Tolstoy preferred 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' over Shakespeare's 'King Lear', and suggests modern critical schools would agree.

book:1205517.description: The gods of Olympus died with the advent of Christianity - or so we have been taught to believe. But how are we to account for their tremendous popularity during the Renaissance? This illustrated book, now reprinted in a new, larger paperback format, offers the general reader a multifaceted look at the far-reaching role played by mythology in Renaissance intellectual and emotional life. After a discussion of mythology in late antiquity and the Middle Ages, Jean Seznec traces the fate of the gods from Bottic...
commentaries: Northrop Frye references this book as a source for allegorical explanations of myths.
Northrop Frye cites Donne's poem as an example of literature using the 'one flesh' metaphor in sexual symbolism.

book:18820247.description: Kalidasa probably lived in the fifth century of the Christian era. This date, approximate as it is, must yet be given with considerable hesitation, and is by no means certain. No truly biographical data are preserved about the author, who nevertheless enjoyed a great popularity during his life, and whom the Hindus have ever regarded as the greatest of Sanskrit poets. We are thus confronted with one of the remarkable problems of literary history. For our ignorance is not due to neglect of Kalidasa's writings...
commentaries: Northrop Frye mentions this play as an example of a comedy where something essential is retrieved from the sea, relating to fishing symbolism.

book:23532908.description:
Translated by Hank Heifetz
Penguin reprint of an earlier edition
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites the work by its title and author as a source.

book:web_840ebcb6.description: A psychoanalytic study of alchemical symbolism and mysticism, translated by Smith Ely Jelliffe. Silberer was an Austrian psychoanalyst and early follower of Freud who applied psychoanalytic principles to esoteric traditions.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book as a source on alchemical symbolism.

book:web_0b486839.description: A prose satire by Elizabethan writer Thomas Lodge, structured around the seven deadly sins and attacking contemporary vices and follies, particularly targeting the playwright and pamphleteer Robert Greene.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Lodge's work as an example of the encyclopaedic, preaching-based form of low-norm satire.

book:978268.description: Contains the text of 'Essay on government' by James Mill, three articles by Macaulay attacking the essay & published in the 'Edinburgh Review' & three replies from the 'Westminster Review'.
commentaries: Northrop Frye uses a sentence from James Mill's 'Essay on Government' as an example of a philosophical style where difficulty is rhetorically motivated by a desire for intellectual honesty and detachment from emotion.

book:web_5bf982d6.description: A critical study of English poetry focusing on the use of articles ('the', 'a', 'an') as stylistic markers, by poet and critic George Rostrevor Hamilton.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references Hamilton's book as a specific study relevant to the preceding point.

book:web_82f3c31d.description: A critical study by Wyndham Lewis analyzing Shakespeare's plays through the archetypes of the lion (representing strength and nobility) and the fox (representing cunning and intelligence), examining heroic roles and political themes.
commentaries: Northrop Frye directs the reader to this book for a discussion of 'Coriolanus'.

book:web_f498cb0c.description: A collection of critical essays by Wyndham Lewis, known for its polemical style and defense of satire and art in the modern age.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references Wyndham Lewis's 'Men Without Art' as a manifesto that accepts the musical analogy in prose, favoring visual aspects (opsis).

book:7905176.description:
Beloved for novels that "deliver laughter, tears, and so much joy" (Romantic Times),JoAnn Ross brings another of Coldwater Cove's citizens to life in this poignant tale of family and friendship, loyalty and loss, courage and suffering. Most of all, this is a story of love's miraculous powers.
FAIR HAVEN
Erin O'Halloran has witnessed the atrocities of war firsthand. But when she travels to Western Ireland to attempt to save a dying friend and mentor, she faces her greatest challenge yet. And when she happens...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book as an example of a literary hoax where fiction is presented as fact, analogous to trompe l'œil in painting.

book:web_d66c7869.description: A three-volume work by anthropologist James Frazer applying comparative folklore and anthropological methods to Old Testament narratives, arguing they contain remnants of earlier primitive beliefs and rituals.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this work as a source for analogues to Biblical stories of the Fall.

book:web_2a5eae66.description: A collection of influential essays on literary theory and criticism, particularly known for the essays "The Intentional Fallacy" and "The Affective Fallacy," which argue against judging a literary work based on authorial intention or reader response.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references a specific chapter in Wimsatt and Beardsley's book as the source for the term 'the intentional fallacy.'

book:web_85150db9.description: A prose satire by Elizabethan writer Thomas Nashe, structured as a complaint to the devil about the vices of society, using the framework of the seven deadly sins.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Nashe's work as an example of the encyclopaedic, preaching-based form of low-norm satire.

book:web_cea0b53c.description: A seminal work of psychoanalytic literary criticism by Otto Rank, analyzing the common pattern in myths of heroic figures. The first edition was published in German in 1909 as 'Der Mythus von der Geburt des Helden'.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book as a detailed study relevant to the archetypal narrative being discussed.

book:web_20175d63.description: A seminal work in psychoanalytic mythology, where Rank analyzes hero birth myths across cultures through a Freudian lens, arguing they follow a common pattern reflecting infantile fantasies.
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites Rank's book as the source for three legends.

book:704004.description:
Along with Adler and Jung, Otto Rank was one of the intellectual giants in the inner circle around Sigmund Freud. Art and Artist, his major statement on the relationship of art to the individual and society, pursues in a broader cultural context Freud's ideas on art and neurosis and has had an important influence on many twentieth-century writers and thinkers, beginning with Henry Miller and Anais Nin.
Art and Artistexplores the human urge to create in all its complex aspects, in terms not only of individua...
commentaries: Joseph Campbell provides a lengthy quotation from Rank's book to support a comparison between neurotic and productive types.

book:8107537.description: Wittgenstein and the Practice of Philosophyintroduces Wittgenstein's philosophy to senior undergraduates and graduate students. Its pedagogical premise is that the best way to understand Wittgenstein's thought is to take seriously his methodological remarks.
commentaries: Northrop Frye acknowledges a debt to a specific passage in Langer's book for the concept of a 'state of naive induction.'

book:817019.description: A failed revolutionary attempt drives the hero of Hudson's novel to seek refuge in the primeval forests of south-western Venezuela. There, in the 'green mansions' of the title, Abel encounters the wood-nymph Rima, the last survivor of a mysterious aboriginal race. The love that flowers between them is soon overshadowed by cruelty and sorrow... One of the acknowledged masters of natural history writing, W. H. Hudson forms an important link between nineteenth-century Romanticism and the twentieth-century ecol...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Hudson's 'Green Mansions' as an example where conventional imagery (a serpent in a paradisal setting) is used without explicit authorial guidance.

book:8507025.description: One of a series of miniature poetry books, each illustrated with wood engravings, published by The Folio Society between 1991 and 1997. This volume, bound in blue-green moire silk with a gold slip case, contains the poems 'The Garden', 'The Picture of little T. C. in a Prospect of Flowers', 'The Mower against Gardens', 'Damon the Mower', 'The Mower to the Glow-worms', 'The Mower's Song', 'The Garden of Appleton House' and 'To His Coy Mistress', illustrated with nine small wood-engravings by Harry Brockway.
commentaries: Northrop Frye analyzes a specific conventional extension of imagery found in Marvell's poem 'The Garden'.

book:662942.description: D. H. Lawrence visited Etruria in April, 1927. It was his "last pilgrimage". There sprang from it a documentary account which is both literary guide and spiritual testament, a global vision of the Etruscan civilization.
commentaries: Northrop Frye compares a point to remarks made by D. H. Lawrence in his book.

book:332435.description: A sequel to the banned novel, The Rainbow, Women in Lovefollows the tumultuous lives of the Brangwen sisters, Gudrun and Ursula. Turning his keen eye on the nature of love, commitment, passion, and marriage, Lawrence gives us the stories of two intelligent, incisive, and observant women, whose temperamental differences spark an ongoing debate regarding their society and their inner lives. The two very different sisters pursue thrilling, torrid affairs; but their quest for more mature emotional relationships...
commentaries: Harold Bloom places Esther Summerson in a literary tradition culminating in the characters from Lawrence's Women in Love.

book:17333168.description:
Set in the rural midlands of England, The Rainbow revolves around three generations of the Brangwen family over a period of more than sixty years, setting them against the emergence of modern England. When Tom Brangwen marries a Polish widow and adopts her daughter as his own, he is unprepared for the conflict and passion that erupt. Suffused with biblical imagery, The Rainbow addresses searching human issues in a setting of precise and vivid detail.
In The Rainbow, D. H. Lawrence challenged the customary l...
commentaries: Harold Bloom cites Frank Kermode's comparison, mentioning D. H. Lawrence's 'The Rainbow' as a book about marriage in its spiritual aspects.

book:591705.description: Lawrence asserted that 'the proper function of a critic is to save the tale from the artist who created it'. In these highly individual, penetrating essays he has exposed 'the American whole soul' within some of that continent's major works of literature. In seeking to establish the status of writings by such authors as Poe, Melville, Fenimore Cooper and Whitman, Lawrence himself has created a classic work. Studies in Classic American Literature is valuable not only for the light it sheds on eighteenth- and...
commentaries: Harold Bloom cites Lawrence's book as a point of comparison for the ambivalent reaction to Whitman's work.

book:1780421.description: Despite being abandoned by his parents, Tom Jones grows into a gallant and irresistible young man. Most of his time is spent romping through the English countryside, getting himself into all kinds of trouble with his good nature and unquenchable eye for women. After being betrayed by jealous relatives, Tom is exiled from home and must undergo a variety of trials in his quest to be reunited with his one true love and to redeem himself in the eyes of society. Filled with mischief and adventure, this bildungsr...
commentaries: Northrop Frye uses Fielding's novel as an example of a work named for its plot, while noting Fielding's strong thematic interest.
Northrop Frye uses Tom Jones as an example of a hero facing a near-catastrophic crisis before a comic resolution.
Northrop Frye mentions Tom Jones as an example where the word 'history' is used in a literary context, though the term has since broadened beyond literature.
Erich Auerbach quotes Henry Fielding's Tom Jones to illustrate the 18th-century convention of treating contemporary everyday life within a comic or satiric mode, not with tragic seriousness.

book:web_29e8940f.description: A popular science book exploring cosmology and the nature of the universe, arguing for a mathematical rather than mechanical understanding of reality.
commentaries: Northrop Frye references Jeans's book to discuss the shift from a mechanical to a mathematical conception of the universe, using it as an analogy for how literature can contain the world within its own autonomous structure.

book:web_325744ee.description: A collection of essays edited by R. S. Crane, containing his influential essay 'The Concept of Plot and the Plot of Tom Jones' along with other works by the Chicago School of criticism.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites Crane's essay in an edited volume for its discussion of plot, specifically in relation to a work being 'named after its plot.'

book:web_23df63b8.description: A collection of lectures by R. S. Crane, a prominent literary critic and leader of the Chicago School of literary criticism, focusing on critical methods and poetic structure.
commentaries: Northrop Frye acknowledges a substantial debt to Crane's book for the theory of the formal phase of criticism.

book:web_b93f8d4d.description: A study examining Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's relationship with and influence on music, including his collaborations with composers and his theories about musical aesthetics.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book for a specific conception of 'parody' in a context where little has been said on a topic.

book:web_8b9c1b0c.description: A collection of essays on English Romantic poetry by the influential poet, critic, and anarchist Sir Herbert Read, focusing on the Romantic emphasis on emotion and imagination.
commentaries: Northrop Frye directs the reader to this book, referenced by its subtitle 'true voice of feeling'.

book:1992003.description: "Edo uparkhei alethine phusike poiese kai ston idion kairo kallitekhnike demiourgia sto olo kai sta kathekasta. Edo aisthanomaste ekeine ten agne eugenikia entupose pou xupna sten psukhe mas monakha to teleios oraio, kathe antithese kataluetai kai xanaphaneronetai e agape, aitia kai desmos kathe pramatou, e nike tes armonias ste nike tou theikou pneumatos. Mesa sten apheleia tou paramuthiou uparkhei ena noema upselotero. To phantastika thaumasto exegietai eukola san poietiko proplasma bathuteron ennoion, ka...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites the Mahabharata as an example of a mythic work containing a full apocalyptic cadence.

book:14781248.description: After seven years of marriage, the beautiful Lady Brenda Last has grown bored with life at Hetton Abbey, the Gothic mansion that is the pride and joy of her husband, Tony. She drifts into an affair with the shallow socialite John Beaver and forsakes Tony for the Belgravia set. In a novel that combines tragedy, comedy, and savage irony, Evelyn Waugh indelibly captures the irresponsible mood of the "crazy and sterile generation" between the wars.
commentaries: Northrop Frye uses the novel as an example of a parody of tragic irony, focusing on the appalling fate of its hero.

book:web_540c5676.description: An anthropological work by German ethnologist Leo Frobenius, translated by A. H. Keane, examining the cultural development of early human societies.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book as a source for analogues to Biblical stories of the Fall.

book:web_cab2e3d2.description: A work by German ethnologist and archaeologist Leo Frobenius, exploring mythological themes related to solar deities. Published as part of his research on cultural history and mythology.
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites Frobenius's work on mythology and the age of the sun god.

book:web_f194942e.description: A two-volume archaeological work documenting prehistoric rock art in the Sahara, published in Munich by Kurt Wolff Verlag. The title refers to a specific site of engraved rock art (Hadjrat Mektouba).
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites this book as the source for an image and description of a Paleolithic petroglyph found in Algiers.

book:web_768df970.description: A major ethnographic work by German explorer and ethnologist Leo Frobenius, presenting his theories on African cultures and civilizations. The full title is often given as 'Und Afrika sprach: Der untergang der atlantisch-kontinent' (And Africa Spoke: The Decline of the Atlantic Continent).
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites specific pages from Frobenius's ethnographic work, comparing its content to a similar episode in Norse mythology.

book:web_db161c84.description: A two-volume scholarly work documenting prehistoric rock art in North Africa, published in Munich by Kurt Wolff Verlag in 1925. The title refers to the 'Written Rock' or 'Inscribed Rock' (Hádschra Máktuba) region.
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites this book as the source for an image and description of a Paleolithic petroglyph found in Algiers.

book:web_30988a4c.description: An ethnological work by German archaeologist and ethnologist Leo Frobenius, exploring African cultures and history.
commentaries: Joseph Campbell cites Frobenius's book.

book:489149.description: First published in 1771, and often regarded as Smollett's finest book, The Expedition of Humphry Clinker relates, in an ingenious series of overlapping letters, the adventures of Mr Matthew Bramble's family party as they travel through England and Scotland. The group includes a gouty country squire, a husband-hunter, an Oxford student, and an illiterate but racy lady's maid. They recount their travelling adventures. They gossip. They tell stories of Humphry Clinker, a servant picked up en route, and they re...
commentaries: Northrop Frye analyzes Humphry Clinker to demonstrate the 'point of ritual death' and subsequent recognition scene in comic plots.

book:6383308.description:
A epopeia imortal que ha quatro seculos vem alimentando a alma portuguesa!
"Os Lusiadas"
Vereis amor da patria, nao movido
De premio vil, mas alto e quase eterno;
Que nao e vil ser conhecido
Por um pregao do ninho meu paterno.
I, 10
commentaries: Northrop Frye lists The Lusiad as an example of a national epic from the high mimetic period, unified by patriotic and religious ideas.

book:web_ef461f32.description: A scholarly work by Lane Cooper analyzing comedy through an Aristotelian framework.
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book in reference to the 'Tractatus Coislinianus'.

book:85530.description: Germans Versus Rome--The Goghic Kingdoms--The Darkness Comes--The Merovingians--The Mayors of the Palace--From Mayor to King--Charlemagne--The Successors of Charlemagne--The End of the Carolingians--The Darkness Begins
commentaries: Northrop Frye states that a quotation from Cassiodorus is sourced from this book.

book:470644.description: From the use of metals by prehistoric man to the alchemical experiments of medieval and renaissance man to the complex chemical skills of contemporary man, Asimov traces the development of this building block of our technological world.
commentaries: Thomas S. Kuhn references Partington's book as a source on the history of chemistry.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book as an example source, alongside another, for remarks on the phlogiston theory.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book as a historical source on chemistry.
Thomas S. Kuhn cites this book for information on the historical problem presented by hydrogen.

book:web_84a95cb4.description: An unfinished epic poem by Abraham Cowley on the biblical story of King David, published in his collected works 'Poems' in 1656.
commentaries: Northrop Frye notes that Cowley demonstrated a persistent interest in imitative harmony, particularly in his work 'Davideis'.

book:2315629.description: His mother is a virgin and he's reputed to be the son of a god; he loses favor and is driven from his kingdom to a sorrowful death -- sound familiar? In The Hero,Lord Raglan contends that the heroic figures from myth and legend are invested with a common pattern that satisfies the human desire for idealization. Raglan outlines 22 characteristic themes or motifs from the heroic tales and illustrates his theory with events from the lives of characters from Oedipus (21 out of a possible 22 points) to Robin Hoo...
commentaries: Northrop Frye cites this book as a reference in a discussion of the 'central unifying myth' of the hero.

book:1403972.description: In this classic study, St. John s Revelation is approached as a great and singular theological poem. Austin Farrer shows how the poem arose in an inspired mind, by what processes of divination its author explored the realm of supernatural truth, how he used the images of his Old Testament faith and gave them fresh meaning in the context of his scheme. Here the reader may follow the workings of a late first-century Christian imagination, in which the Scriptures and the stars, the liturgy of the temple and th...
commentaries: Northrop Frye recommends this book as a useful source on Biblical typology.

book:web_953bbef4.description: A critical work by poet and critic Donald Davie examining poetic syntax and its relationship to meaning and form in English poetry.
